   192	/-! ## The cubic Fourier identity -/
   193	
   194	/-- Formalization-only auxiliary lemma for the Fourier computations in the
   195	proof of Theorem 10 of Natarajan--Vidick
   196	(`references/nv-paper/fullpaper.tex:1096-1112`): a twisted form of the
   197	matrix-valued Parseval identity in which only the first factor is expanded
   198	through its Fourier coefficients.  Taking `a = 0` recovers Parseval. -/
   199	private theorem sum_booleanCharacter_smul_operatorFourier_mul {t : ℕ}
   200	    {ι : Type} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
   201	    (A X : (Fin t → ZMod 2) → Op ι) (a : Fin t → ZMod 2) :
   202	    ∑ u : Fin t → ZMod 2,
   203	        booleanCharacter u a • (operatorFourier A u * X u) =
   204	      ((Fintype.card (Fin t → ZMod 2) : ℂ)⁻¹) •
   205	        ∑ b : Fin t → ZMod 2,
   206	          A b * ∑ u : Fin t → ZMod 2, booleanCharacter u (a + b) • X u := by
   207	  classical
   208	  let N : ℂ := Fintype.card (Fin t → ZMod 2)
   209	  calc
   210	    ∑ u : Fin t → ZMod 2,
   211	        booleanCharacter u a • (operatorFourier A u * X u) =
   212	        ∑ u : Fin t → ZMod 2, N⁻¹ • ∑ b : Fin t → ZMod 2,
   213	          booleanCharacter u (a + b) • (A b * X u) := by
   214	      apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
   215	      intro u _
   216	      simp only [operatorFourier, N, smul_mul_assoc, Finset.sum_mul,
   217	        Finset.smul_sum, smul_smul, booleanCharacter_add_right]
   218	      apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
   219	      intro b _
   220	      congr 1
   221	      ring
   222	    _ = N⁻¹ • ∑ b : Fin t → ZMod 2, ∑ u : Fin t → ZMod 2,
   223	          booleanCharacter u (a + b) • (A b * X u) := by
   224	      rw [← Finset.smul_sum]
   225	      congr 1
   226	      exact Finset.sum_comm
   227	    _ = N⁻¹ • ∑ b : Fin t → ZMod 2,
   228	          A b * ∑ u : Fin t → ZMod 2, booleanCharacter u (a + b) • X u := by
   229	      congr 1
   230	      apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
   231	      intro b _
   232	      rw [Finset.mul_sum]
   233	      apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
   234	      intro u _
   235	      rw [mul_smul_comm]
   236	
   237	/-- The sum of the cubes of the Fourier coefficients of an operator family is
   238	the average of `O^a O^b O^{a+b}` over a uniformly random pair `(a, b)`.  This
   239	is the operator form of the identity
   240	`∑_u (hat A^u)^3 = E_{a,b} A(a) A(b) A(a+b)` invoked at
   241	`references/nv-paper/fullpaper.tex:1111-1112`; the order of the three factors
   242	is preserved throughout. -/
   243	theorem sum_operatorFourier_cube {t : ℕ} {ι : Type} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
   244	    (O : (Fin t → ZMod 2) → Op ι) :
   245	    ∑ u : Fin t → ZMod 2,
   246	        operatorFourier O u * operatorFourier O u * operatorFourier O u =
   247	      ((Fintype.card ((Fin t → ZMod 2) × (Fin t → ZMod 2)) : ℂ)⁻¹) •
   248	        ∑ p : (Fin t → ZMod 2) × (Fin t → ZMod 2),
   249	          O p.1 * O p.2 * O (p.1 + p.2) := by
   250	  classical
   251	  let N : ℂ := Fintype.card (Fin t → ZMod 2)
   252	  have hinner : ∀ b : Fin t → ZMod 2,
   253	      ∑ u : Fin t → ZMod 2,
   254	          booleanCharacter u b • (operatorFourier O u * operatorFourier O u) =
   255	        N⁻¹ • ∑ c : Fin t → ZMod 2, O c * O (b + c) := by
   256	    intro b
   257	    rw [sum_booleanCharacter_smul_operatorFourier_mul]
   258	    congr 1
   259	    apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
   260	    intro c _
   261	    rw [operatorFourier_inversion]
   262	  calc
   263	    ∑ u : Fin t → ZMod 2,
   264	        operatorFourier O u * operatorFourier O u * operatorFourier O u =
   265	        ∑ u : Fin t → ZMod 2, booleanCharacter u 0 •
   266	          (operatorFourier O u * (operatorFourier O u * operatorFourier O u)) := by
   267	      apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
   268	      intro u _
   269	      rw [booleanCharacter_zero_right, one_smul, Matrix.mul_assoc]
   270	    _ = N⁻¹ • ∑ b : Fin t → ZMod 2, O b * ∑ u : Fin t → ZMod 2,
   271	          booleanCharacter u (0 + b) •
   272	            (operatorFourier O u * operatorFourier O u) := by
   273	      rw [sum_booleanCharacter_smul_operatorFourier_mul]
   274	    _ = N⁻¹ • ∑ b : Fin t → ZMod 2,
   275	          O b * (N⁻¹ • ∑ c : Fin t → ZMod 2, O c * O (b + c)) := by
   276	      simp only [zero_add, hinner]
   277	    _ = (N⁻¹ * N⁻¹) • ∑ b : Fin t → ZMod 2, ∑ c : Fin t → ZMod 2,
   278	          O b * O c * O (b + c) := by
   279	      simp only [mul_smul_comm, Finset.mul_sum, ← Finset.smul_sum, smul_smul,
   280	        Matrix.mul_assoc]
   281	    _ = ((Fintype.card ((Fin t → ZMod 2) × (Fin t → ZMod 2)) : ℂ)⁻¹) •
   282	          ∑ p : (Fin t → ZMod 2) × (Fin t → ZMod 2),
   283	            O p.1 * O p.2 * O (p.1 + p.2) := by
   284	      rw [Fintype.sum_prod_type, Fintype.card_prod, Nat.cast_mul, mul_inv]
   285	
   286	/-- Formalization-only auxiliary lemma for the averages in this file: a uniform
   287	average over a nonempty finite type is the sum divided by the cardinality. -/
   288	private theorem avgOver_uniform_eq_inv_card_mul_sum {α : Type*}
   289	    [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α] [Nonempty α] (f : α → ℝ) :
   290	    avgOver (uniformDistribution α) f = (Fintype.card α : ℝ)⁻¹ * ∑ a, f a := by
   291	  simp [avgOver, uniformDistribution, Distribution.uniformOnFinset_weight,
   292	    Finset.mul_sum]
   293	
   294	/-- The sum of the cubic Fourier coefficients evaluated in `ρ` equals the
   295	two-query correlation:
   296	`∑_u Re Tr((hat O^u)^3 ρ) = E_{a,b} Re Tr(O^a O^b O^{a+b} ρ)`.  This is the
   297	identity stated at `references/nv-paper/fullpaper.tex:1111-1112`, with the
   298	complex traces compared through their real parts. -/
   299	theorem operatorFourier_cube_trace_eq_correlation {t : ℕ}
   300	    {ι : Type} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
   301	    (O : (Fin t → ZMod 2) → Op ι) (ρ : Op ι) :
   302	    ∑ u : Fin t → ZMod 2,
   303	        (Matrix.trace (operatorFourier O u * operatorFourier O u *
   304	          operatorFourier O u * ρ)).re =
   305	      blrCorrelation O ρ := by
   306	  rw [← Complex.re_sum, ← Matrix.trace_sum, ← Finset.sum_mul,
   307	    sum_operatorFourier_cube, smul_mul_assoc, Matrix.trace_smul, Finset.sum_mul,
   308	    Matrix.trace_sum]
   309	  unfold blrCorrelation
   310	  rw [avgOver_uniform_eq_inv_card_mul_sum, smul_eq_mul, ← Complex.ofReal_natCast,
   311	    ← Complex.ofReal_inv, Complex.re_ofReal_mul, Complex.re_sum]
   312	
   313	/-! ## The Fourier-square POVM and its overlap certificate -/
   314	
   315	/-- Each Fourier square `B^u = (hat O^u)^2` of a Hermitian operator family is
   316	positive semidefinite, being the product of a Hermitian matrix with its
   317	adjoint.  This is the positivity half of the assertion that the `B^u` form a
   318	POVM at `references/nv-paper/fullpaper.tex:1098-1099`. -/
   319	theorem operatorFourier_mul_self_posSemidef {t : ℕ}
   320	    {ι : Type} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
   321	    (O : (Fin t → ZMod 2) → Op ι) (hO : ∀ a, (O a).IsHermitian)
   322	    (u : Fin t → ZMod 2) :
   323	    (operatorFourier O u * operatorFourier O u).PosSemidef := by
   324	  have h := operatorFourier_isHermitian O hO u
   325	  simpa [h.eq] using
   326	    Matrix.posSemidef_conjTranspose_mul_self (operatorFourier O u)
   327	
   328	/-- The Fourier-square POVM `{B^u = (hat O^u)^2}` of a family of binary
   329	observables, with outcomes in `𝔽_2^t`.  Positivity is
   330	`operatorFourier_mul_self_posSemidef` and completeness is the Parseval
   331	identity `sum_operatorFourier_sq_eq_one`.  This is the POVM to which Naimark's
   332	theorem is applied at `references/nv-paper/fullpaper.tex:1097-1100`. -/
   333	def fourierSquareMeasurement {t : ℕ} {ι : Type} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
   334	    (O : (Fin t → ZMod 2) → Op ι) (hO : ∀ a, IsBinaryObservable (O a)) :
   335	    Measurement (Fin t → ZMod 2) ι :=
   336	  Measurement.ofSumEqOne
   337	    (fun u => operatorFourier O u * operatorFourier O u)
   338	    (fun u => (operatorFourier_mul_self_posSemidef O (fun a => (hO a).1) u).nonneg)
   339	    (sum_operatorFourier_sq_eq_one O hO)
   340	
   341	/-- The effects of the Fourier-square POVM are the squares of the Fourier
   342	coefficients. -/
   343	@[simp]
   344	theorem fourierSquareMeasurement_effect {t : ℕ}
   345	    {ι : Type} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
   346	    (O : (Fin t → ZMod 2) → Op ι) (hO : ∀ a, IsBinaryObservable (O a))
   347	    (u : Fin t → ZMod 2) :
   348	    (fourierSquareMeasurement O hO).effect u =
   349	      operatorFourier O u * operatorFourier O u :=
   350	  rfl
   351	
   352	/-- The average state-dependent overlap between `O^a` and the character sum
   353	`∑_u (-1)^{u·a} B^u` of the Fourier-square operators `B^u = (hat O^u)^2` equals
   354	the sum of the cubic Fourier coefficients evaluated in `ρ`.  The family `O` is
   355	arbitrary here, so the `B^u` need not be positive or sum to the identity; they
   356	are the effects of a POVM only under the binary-observable hypothesis of
   357	`fourierSquareMeasurement`.  This is the computation of
   358	`E_a Re Tr_{ρ'}(A(a) 𝒜(a))` at `references/nv-paper/fullpaper.tex:1104-1110`,
   359	carried out before the Naimark dilation: the character sum is the compression
   360	of the exactly linear observable `𝒜(a) = ∑_u (-1)^{u·a} C^u` to the original
   361	space. -/
   362	theorem avg_overlap_fourierSquare_eq_sum_cube {t : ℕ}
   363	    {ι : Type} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
   364	    (O : (Fin t → ZMod 2) → Op ι) (ρ : Op ι) :
   365	    avgOver (uniformDistribution (Fin t → ZMod 2))
   366	        (fun a => (Matrix.trace (O a *
   367	          (∑ u : Fin t → ZMod 2, booleanCharacter u a •
   368	            (operatorFourier O u * operatorFourier O u)) * ρ)).re) =
   369	      ∑ u : Fin t → ZMod 2,
   370	        (Matrix.trace (operatorFourier O u * operatorFourier O u *
   371	          operatorFourier O u * ρ)).re := by
   372	  classical
   373	  have hop :
   374	      ∑ u : Fin t → ZMod 2,
   375	          operatorFourier O u * (operatorFourier O u * operatorFourier O u) =
   376	        ((Fintype.card (Fin t → ZMod 2) : ℂ)⁻¹) •
   377	          ∑ b : Fin t → ZMod 2, O b * ∑ u : Fin t → ZMod 2,
   378	            booleanCharacter u b • (operatorFourier O u * operatorFourier O u) := by
   379	    have := sum_booleanCharacter_smul_operatorFourier_mul O
   380	      (fun u => operatorFourier O u * operatorFourier O u) 0
   381	    simpa only [booleanCharacter_zero_right, one_smul, zero_add] using this
   382	  symm
   383	  calc
   384	    ∑ u : Fin t → ZMod 2,
   385	        (Matrix.trace (operatorFourier O u * operatorFourier O u *
   386	          operatorFourier O u * ρ)).re =
   387	        (Matrix.trace ((∑ u : Fin t → ZMod 2,
   388	          operatorFourier O u * (operatorFourier O u * operatorFourier O u)) *
   389	            ρ)).re := by
   390	      rw [Finset.sum_mul, Matrix.trace_sum, Complex.re_sum]
   391	      simp only [Matrix.mul_assoc]
   392	    _ = (Matrix.trace ((((Fintype.card (Fin t → ZMod 2) : ℂ)⁻¹) •
   393	          ∑ b : Fin t → ZMod 2, O b * ∑ u : Fin t → ZMod 2,
   394	            booleanCharacter u b • (operatorFourier O u * operatorFourier O u)) *
   395	              ρ)).re := by
   396	      rw [hop]
   397	    _ = (Fintype.card (Fin t → ZMod 2) : ℝ)⁻¹ *
   398	          ∑ b : Fin t → ZMod 2, (Matrix.trace (O b *
   399	            (∑ u : Fin t → ZMod 2, booleanCharacter u b •
   400	              (operatorFourier O u * operatorFourier O u)) * ρ)).re := by
   401	      rw [smul_mul_assoc, Matrix.trace_smul, Finset.sum_mul, Matrix.trace_sum,
   402	        smul_eq_mul, ← Complex.ofReal_natCast, ← Complex.ofReal_inv,
   403	        Complex.re_ofReal_mul, Complex.re_sum]
   404	    _ = avgOver (uniformDistribution (Fin t → ZMod 2))
   405	          (fun a => (Matrix.trace (O a *
   406	            (∑ u : Fin t → ZMod 2, booleanCharacter u a •
   407	              (operatorFourier O u * operatorFourier O u)) * ρ)).re) := by
   408	      rw [avgOver_uniform_eq_inv_card_mul_sum]

   420	theorem one_sub_error_le_avg_overlap_fourierSquare {t : ℕ}
   421	    {ι : Type} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
   422	    (O : (Fin t → ZMod 2) → Op ι) (ρ : Op ι)

     4	/-!
     5	# Boolean Fourier analysis for the quantum linearity theorem
     6	
     7	This file develops the finite Fourier identities used in the proof of the
     8	quantum linearity theorem.  The Boolean characters are the additive characters
     9	of `𝔽_2^t`; their orthogonality gives Fourier inversion and matrix-valued
    10	Parseval for operator families.  The final section records the normalization
    11	relating the state-dependent operator distance to the distance between the
    12	associated binary projective measurements.
    13	
    14	## References
    15	
    16	The Fourier and Parseval argument is Theorem 10, equations (7)--(8), and its
    17	proof in `references/nv-paper/fullpaper.tex:1074-1112`.  The observable-distance
    18	calculation is in the same source at lines 900--912.  The QPBT paper invokes
    19	this theorem in
    20	`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:711-725`.
    21	-/
    22	
    23	open scoped BigOperators Matrix MatrixOrder ComplexOrder
    24	
    25	namespace MIPStarRE.QPBT
    26	
    27	open MIPStarRE.LDT
    28	open MIPStarRE.Quantum
    29	
    30	noncomputable section
    31	
    32	/-! ## Boolean characters -/
    33	
    34	/-- The character `a |-> (-1)^(a dot u)` on the Boolean cube `𝔽_2^t`.
    35	
    36	This is the scalar character used in the Fourier transform at
    37	`references/nv-paper/fullpaper.tex:1095-1098`. -/
    38	noncomputable def booleanCharacter {t : ℕ}
    39	    (u a : Fin t → ZMod 2) : ℂ :=
    40	  MIPStarRE.LDT.Preliminaries.ffVecChar (p := 2) (F := ZMod 2) u a
    41	
    42	/-- Formalization-only auxiliary lemma for the Fourier transform at
    43	`references/nv-paper/fullpaper.tex:1095-1098`: a Boolean character is
    44	multiplicative in its argument. -/
    45	theorem booleanCharacter_add_right {t : ℕ} (u a b : Fin t → ZMod 2) :
    46	    booleanCharacter u (a + b) = booleanCharacter u a * booleanCharacter u b := by
    47	  exact AddChar.map_add_eq_mul
    48	    (MIPStarRE.LDT.Preliminaries.ffVecChar (p := 2) (F := ZMod 2) u) a b
    49	
    50	/-- Formalization-only auxiliary lemma for the Fourier transform at
    51	`references/nv-paper/fullpaper.tex:1095-1098`: the Boolean pairing defining
    52	the characters is symmetric. -/
    53	theorem booleanCharacter_comm {t : ℕ} (u a : Fin t → ZMod 2) :
    54	    booleanCharacter u a = booleanCharacter a u := by
    55	  simp only [booleanCharacter, MIPStarRE.LDT.Preliminaries.ffVecChar_apply]
    56	  have hdot : MIPStarRE.LDT.Preliminaries.ffDotProduct a u =
    57	      MIPStarRE.LDT.Preliminaries.ffDotProduct u a := by
    58	    unfold MIPStarRE.LDT.Preliminaries.ffDotProduct
    59	    apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
    60	    intro i _
    61	    exact mul_comm _ _
    62	  rw [hdot]
    63	
    64	/-- Formalization-only auxiliary lemma for the Fourier transform at
    65	`references/nv-paper/fullpaper.tex:1095-1098`: a Boolean character is
    66	multiplicative in its frequency. -/
    67	theorem booleanCharacter_add_left {t : ℕ} (u v a : Fin t → ZMod 2) :
    68	    booleanCharacter (u + v) a = booleanCharacter u a * booleanCharacter v a := by
    69	  rw [booleanCharacter_comm, booleanCharacter_add_right]
    70	  rw [booleanCharacter_comm a u, booleanCharacter_comm a v]
    71	
    72	/-- Formalization-only auxiliary lemma for the Fourier transform at
    73	`references/nv-paper/fullpaper.tex:1095-1098`: a Boolean character takes
    74	the value one at the zero argument. -/
    75	@[simp]
    76	theorem booleanCharacter_zero_right {t : ℕ} (u : Fin t → ZMod 2) :
    77	    booleanCharacter u 0 = 1 := by
    78	  change MIPStarRE.LDT.Preliminaries.ffVecChar (p := 2) (F := ZMod 2) u 0 = 1
    79	  exact AddChar.map_zero_eq_one _
    80	
    81	/-- Formalization-only auxiliary lemma for the Fourier transform at
    82	`references/nv-paper/fullpaper.tex:1095-1098`: a Boolean character takes
    83	the value one at the zero frequency. -/
    84	@[simp]
    85	theorem booleanCharacter_zero_left {t : ℕ} (a : Fin t → ZMod 2) :
    86	    booleanCharacter 0 a = 1 := by
    87	  rw [booleanCharacter_comm]
    88	  exact booleanCharacter_zero_right a

    90	/-- Formalization-only auxiliary lemma for the Fourier transform at
    91	`references/nv-paper/fullpaper.tex:1095-1098`: every Boolean character
    92	takes values whose square is one. -/
    93	theorem booleanCharacter_mul_self {t : ℕ} (u a : Fin t → ZMod 2) :
    94	    booleanCharacter u a * booleanCharacter u a = 1 := by
    95	  rw [← booleanCharacter_add_right]
    96	  have haa : a + a = 0 := by
    97	    ext i
    98	    exact CharTwo.add_self_eq_zero (a i)
    99	  rw [haa, booleanCharacter_zero_right]

   101	/-- Formalization-only auxiliary lemma for the Fourier transform at
   102	`references/nv-paper/fullpaper.tex:1095-1098`: Boolean characters are real,
   103	hence fixed by complex conjugation. -/
   104	theorem star_booleanCharacter {t : ℕ} (u a : Fin t → ZMod 2) :
   105	    star (booleanCharacter u a) = booleanCharacter u a := by
   106	  rcases mul_self_eq_one_iff.mp (booleanCharacter_mul_self u a) with h | h
   107	  · simp [h]
   108	  · simp [h]
   109	
   110	/-- Formalization-only auxiliary lemma for the Fourier transform at
   111	`references/nv-paper/fullpaper.tex:1095-1098`: the unnormalized character
   112	sum vanishes away from frequency zero. -/
   113	theorem sum_booleanCharacter {t : ℕ} (u : Fin t → ZMod 2) :
   114	    ∑ a : Fin t → ZMod 2, booleanCharacter u a =
   115	      if u = 0 then (Fintype.card (Fin t → ZMod 2) : ℂ) else 0 := by
   116	  rw [show (∑ a : Fin t → ZMod 2, booleanCharacter u a) =
   117	      (Fintype.card (Fin t → ZMod 2) : ℂ) *
   118	        𝔼 a : Fin t → ZMod 2, booleanCharacter u a by
   119	    rw [Fintype.expect_eq_sum_div_card]
   120	    field_simp]
   121	  rw [show (𝔼 a : Fin t → ZMod 2, booleanCharacter u a) =
   122	      if u = 0 then (1 : ℂ) else 0 by
   123	    simpa [booleanCharacter] using
   124	      (MIPStarRE.LDT.Preliminaries.fourier_fact_vector
   125	        (p := 2) (F := ZMod 2) u)]
   126	  split_ifs <;> simp
   127	
   128	/-- Formalization-only auxiliary lemma for the Fourier transform at
   129	`references/nv-paper/fullpaper.tex:1095-1098`: summing a character over
   130	frequencies gives the delta function at zero. -/
   131	theorem sum_booleanCharacter_swap {t : ℕ} (a : Fin t → ZMod 2) :
   132	    ∑ u : Fin t → ZMod 2, booleanCharacter u a =
   133	      if a = 0 then (Fintype.card (Fin t → ZMod 2) : ℂ) else 0 := by
   134	  simpa only [booleanCharacter_comm] using sum_booleanCharacter a
   135	
   136	/-- Formalization-only auxiliary lemma for the Fourier transform at
   137	`references/nv-paper/fullpaper.tex:1095-1098`: orthogonality of two Boolean
   138	characters, in the form used by Fourier inversion and Parseval. -/
   139	theorem sum_booleanCharacter_mul {t : ℕ} (a b : Fin t → ZMod 2) :
   140	    ∑ u : Fin t → ZMod 2, booleanCharacter u a * booleanCharacter u b =
   141	      if a = b then (Fintype.card (Fin t → ZMod 2) : ℂ) else 0 := by
   142	  rw [← Finset.sum_congr rfl (fun u _ => booleanCharacter_add_right u a b)]
   143	  rw [sum_booleanCharacter_swap]
   144	  have hab : a + b = 0 ↔ a = b := by
   145	    constructor
   146	    · intro h
   147	      have := congrFun h
   148	      funext i
   149	      have hi := this i
   150	      exact (CharTwo.add_eq_zero.mp hi)
   151	    · intro h
   152	      subst b
   153	      ext i
   154	      exact CharTwo.add_self_eq_zero (a i)
   155	  simp only [hab]
   156	
   157	/-! ## Operator-valued Fourier analysis -/
   158	
   159	/-- The normalized Fourier coefficient of an operator family on the Boolean
   160	cube.  This is `hat A^u = E_a (-1)^(a dot u) A(a)` from
   161	`references/nv-paper/fullpaper.tex:1095-1098`. -/
   162	noncomputable def operatorFourier {t : ℕ} {ι : Type*}
   163	    [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
   164	    (O : (Fin t → ZMod 2) → Op ι) (u : Fin t → ZMod 2) : Op ι :=
   165	  ((Fintype.card (Fin t → ZMod 2) : ℂ)⁻¹) •
   166	    ∑ a : Fin t → ZMod 2, booleanCharacter u a • O a
   167	
   168	/-- Formalization-only auxiliary lemma for the Fourier argument at
   169	`references/nv-paper/fullpaper.tex:1095-1100`: Fourier coefficients of a
   170	Hermitian operator family are Hermitian. -/
   171	theorem operatorFourier_isHermitian {t : ℕ} {ι : Type*}
   172	    [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
   173	    (O : (Fin t → ZMod 2) → Op ι) (hO : ∀ a, (O a).IsHermitian)
   174	    (u : Fin t → ZMod 2) :
   175	    (operatorFourier O u).IsHermitian := by
   176	  rw [Matrix.IsHermitian]
   177	  simp only [operatorFourier, Matrix.conjTranspose_smul,
   178	    Matrix.conjTranspose_sum, star_inv₀, star_natCast]
   179	  congr 1
   180	  apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
   181	  intro a _
   182	  rw [star_booleanCharacter, (hO a).eq]
   183	
   184	/-- Formalization-only auxiliary lemma for the Fourier argument at
   185	`references/nv-paper/fullpaper.tex:1095-1100`: Fourier inversion for
   186	operator-valued functions on the Boolean cube. -/
   187	theorem operatorFourier_inversion {t : ℕ} {ι : Type*}
   188	    [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
   189	    (O : (Fin t → ZMod 2) → Op ι) (a : Fin t → ZMod 2) :
   190	    ∑ u : Fin t → ZMod 2, booleanCharacter u a • operatorFourier O u = O a := by
   191	  classical
   192	  let N : ℂ := Fintype.card (Fin t → ZMod 2)
   193	  have hN : N ≠ 0 := by
   194	    simp [N]
   195	  calc
   196	    ∑ u : Fin t → ZMod 2, booleanCharacter u a • operatorFourier O u =
   197	        ∑ u : Fin t → ZMod 2, ∑ b : Fin t → ZMod 2,
   198	          (booleanCharacter u a * N⁻¹ * booleanCharacter u b) • O b := by
   199	      apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
   200	      intro u _
   201	      simp only [operatorFourier, N, smul_smul, Finset.smul_sum]
   202	      apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
   203	      intro b _
   204	      rw [mul_assoc]
   205	    _ = ∑ b : Fin t → ZMod 2, ∑ u : Fin t → ZMod 2,
   206	          (booleanCharacter u a * N⁻¹ * booleanCharacter u b) • O b := by
   207	      rw [Finset.sum_comm]
   208	    _ = N⁻¹ • ∑ b : Fin t → ZMod 2,
   209	          (∑ u : Fin t → ZMod 2,
   210	            booleanCharacter u a * booleanCharacter u b) • O b := by
   211	      rw [Finset.smul_sum]
   212	      apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
   213	      intro b _
   214	      rw [smul_smul, ← Finset.sum_smul, Finset.mul_sum]
   215	      apply congrArg (fun c : ℂ => c • O b)
   216	      apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
   217	      intro u _
   218	      ring
   219	    _ = N⁻¹ • ∑ b : Fin t → ZMod 2,
   220	          (if a = b then N else 0) • O b := by
   221	      congr 1
   222	      apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
   223	      intro b _
   224	      rw [sum_booleanCharacter_mul]
   225	    _ = O a := by
   226	      simp [hN]
   227	
   228	/-- Formalization-only auxiliary lemma for the Fourier argument at
   229	`references/nv-paper/fullpaper.tex:1095-1100`: the matrix-valued Parseval
   230	identity for the Boolean Fourier transform.  The order of the two operator
   231	families is preserved. -/
   232	theorem sum_operatorFourier_mul_operatorFourier {t : ℕ} {ι : Type*}
   233	    [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
   234	    (A B : (Fin t → ZMod 2) → Op ι) :
   235	    ∑ u : Fin t → ZMod 2, operatorFourier A u * operatorFourier B u =
   236	      ((Fintype.card (Fin t → ZMod 2) : ℂ)⁻¹) •
   237	        ∑ a : Fin t → ZMod 2, A a * B a := by
   238	  classical
   239	  let N : ℂ := Fintype.card (Fin t → ZMod 2)
   240	  calc
   241	    ∑ u : Fin t → ZMod 2, operatorFourier A u * operatorFourier B u =
   242	        ∑ u : Fin t → ZMod 2, N⁻¹ •
   243	          ∑ a : Fin t → ZMod 2,
   244	            (booleanCharacter u a • A a) * operatorFourier B u := by
   245	      apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
   246	      intro u _
   247	      change (N⁻¹ • ∑ a : Fin t → ZMod 2, booleanCharacter u a • A a) *
   248	          operatorFourier B u = _
   249	      rw [smul_mul_assoc, Finset.sum_mul]
   250	    _ = N⁻¹ • ∑ u : Fin t → ZMod 2, ∑ a : Fin t → ZMod 2,
   251	          (booleanCharacter u a • A a) * operatorFourier B u := by
   252	      rw [Finset.smul_sum]
   253	    _ = N⁻¹ • ∑ a : Fin t → ZMod 2, ∑ u : Fin t → ZMod 2,
   254	          (booleanCharacter u a • A a) * operatorFourier B u := by
   255	      congr 1
   256	      rw [Finset.sum_comm]
   257	    _ = N⁻¹ • ∑ a : Fin t → ZMod 2,
   258	          A a * (∑ u : Fin t → ZMod 2,
   259	            booleanCharacter u a • operatorFourier B u) := by
   260	      congr 1
   261	      apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
   262	      intro a _
   263	      rw [Finset.mul_sum]
   264	      apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
   265	      intro u _
   266	      rw [smul_mul_assoc, mul_smul_comm]
   267	    _ = N⁻¹ • ∑ a : Fin t → ZMod 2, A a * B a := by
   268	      congr 1
   269	      apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
   270	      intro a _
   271	      rw [operatorFourier_inversion]
   272	    _ = ((Fintype.card (Fin t → ZMod 2) : ℂ)⁻¹) •
   273	          ∑ a : Fin t → ZMod 2, A a * B a := by
   274	      rfl
   275	
   276	/-- Formalization-only auxiliary lemma for the Fourier argument at
   277	`references/nv-paper/fullpaper.tex:1095-1100`: Parseval specialized to the
   278	square of a single operator family. -/
   279	theorem sum_operatorFourier_sq {t : ℕ} {ι : Type*}
   280	    [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
   281	    (O : (Fin t → ZMod 2) → Op ι) :
   282	    ∑ u : Fin t → ZMod 2, operatorFourier O u * operatorFourier O u =
   283	      ((Fintype.card (Fin t → ZMod 2) : ℂ)⁻¹) •
   284	        ∑ a : Fin t → ZMod 2, O a * O a :=
   285	  sum_operatorFourier_mul_operatorFourier O O
   286	
   287	/-- For a family of binary observables, the squares of the Fourier
   288	coefficients sum to the identity.  This is the Parseval step asserting that
   289	`B^u = (hat A^u)^2` is a POVM in
   290	`references/nv-paper/fullpaper.tex:1096-1100`. -/
   291	theorem sum_operatorFourier_sq_eq_one {t : ℕ} {ι : Type}
   292	    [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
   293	    (O : (Fin t → ZMod 2) → Op ι)
   294	    (hO : ∀ a, IsBinaryObservable (O a)) :
   295	    ∑ u : Fin t → ZMod 2, operatorFourier O u * operatorFourier O u = 1 := by
   296	  rw [sum_operatorFourier_sq]
   297	  simp_rw [(hO _).2]
   298	  rw [Finset.sum_const]
   299	  rw [← Nat.cast_smul_eq_nsmul ℂ]
   300	  rw [smul_smul]
   301	  simp
   302	
   303	/-! ## Observable-distance normalization -/
   304	
   305	/-- The affine operator `(1 ± S)/2`, which is the effect of a binary projective
   306	measurement when `S` is a binary observable.
   307	The two effects are `(1 + O) / 2` and `(1 - O) / 2`. -/
   308	noncomputable def binaryObservableEffect {ι : Type} [Fintype ι]
   309	    [DecidableEq ι] (outcome : Bool) (O : Op ι) : Op ι :=
   310	  if outcome then ((2 : ℂ)⁻¹) • (1 - O) else ((2 : ℂ)⁻¹) • (1 + O)
   311	
   312	/-- The squared binary-measurement distance of two operators, summed over the two
   313	effects `(1 ± O)/2`; when both operators are binary observables this is the
   314	squared distance between the associated binary projective measurements.  This is the measurement
   315	distance calculated in `references/nv-paper/fullpaper.tex:900-912`; its relation
   316	to `stateDepDistSq` is recorded in
   317	`docs/paper-gaps/qpbt_linearity-distance-normalization.tex`. -/
   318	noncomputable def binaryObservableDistSq {ι : Type} [Fintype ι]
   319	    [DecidableEq ι] (S T ρ : Op ι) : ℝ :=
   320	  ∑ outcome : Bool,
   321	    stateDepDistSq (binaryObservableEffect outcome S)
   322	      (binaryObservableEffect outcome T) ρ
   323	
   324	/-- The squared binary-measurement distance is half the squared
   325	state-dependent operator distance.
   326	
   327	**Local fix:** Source equation (3) at
   328	`references/nv-paper/fullpaper.tex:903-911` ends by identifying the squared
   329	binary-measurement distance with the squared state-dependent operator distance
   330	of the two observables; the correct relation carries the factor `1 / 2` proved
   331	here.
   332	Documented in
   333	`docs/paper-gaps/qpbt_linearity-distance-normalization.tex`. -/
   334	theorem binaryObservableDistSq_eq_stateDepDistSq_div_two
   335	    {ι : Type} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] (S T ρ : Op ι) :
   336	    binaryObservableDistSq S T ρ = stateDepDistSq S T ρ / 2 := by
   337	  simp only [binaryObservableDistSq, Fintype.univ_bool, stateDepDistSq,
   338	    binaryObservableEffect, smul_add, Matrix.conjTranspose_sub,
   339	    Finset.mem_singleton, Bool.true_eq_false, not_false_eq_true,
   340	    Finset.sum_insert, reduceIte, Matrix.conjTranspose_smul, star_inv₀,
   341	    star_ofNat, Matrix.conjTranspose_one, Finset.sum_singleton,
   342	    Bool.false_eq_true, Matrix.conjTranspose_add, add_sub_add_left_eq_sub]
   343	  have hminusStar :
   344	      (2 : ℂ)⁻¹ • (1 - Sᴴ) - (2 : ℂ)⁻¹ • (1 - Tᴴ) =
   345	        -((2 : ℂ)⁻¹ • (Sᴴ - Tᴴ)) := by
   346	    module
   347	  have hminus :
   348	      (2 : ℂ)⁻¹ • (1 - S) - (2 : ℂ)⁻¹ • (1 - T) =
   349	        -((2 : ℂ)⁻¹ • (S - T)) := by
   350	    module
   351	  have hplusStar :
   352	      (2 : ℂ)⁻¹ • Sᴴ - (2 : ℂ)⁻¹ • Tᴴ =
   353	        (2 : ℂ)⁻¹ • (Sᴴ - Tᴴ) := by
   354	    module
   355	  have hplus :
   356	      (2 : ℂ)⁻¹ • S - (2 : ℂ)⁻¹ • T =
   357	        (2 : ℂ)⁻¹ • (S - T) := by
   358	    module
   359	  rw [hminusStar, hminus, hplusStar, hplus]
   360	  simp only [neg_mul, mul_neg, neg_neg, smul_mul_assoc, Matrix.trace_smul]
   361	  norm_num [Complex.mul_re]
   362	  ring
   363	
   364	/-- The state-dependent squared distance between binary observables in terms
   365	of their correlation. -/
   366	theorem stateDepDistSq_eq_two_sub_two_mul_correlation
   367	    {ι : Type} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
   368	    (S T ρ : Op ι) (hS : IsBinaryObservable S)
   369	    (hT : IsBinaryObservable T) (hρ : ρ.PosSemidef)
   370	    (htrace : Matrix.trace ρ = 1) :
   371	    stateDepDistSq S T ρ =
   372	      2 - 2 * (Matrix.trace (S * T * ρ)).re := by
   373	  have hstar :
   374	      star (Matrix.trace (S * T * ρ)) = Matrix.trace (T * S * ρ) := by
   375	    calc
   376	      star (Matrix.trace (S * T * ρ)) = Matrix.trace ((S * T * ρ)ᴴ) := by
   377	        rw [Matrix.trace_conjTranspose]
   378	      _ = Matrix.trace (ρ * T * S) := by
   379	        simp [Matrix.conjTranspose_mul, hS.1.eq, hT.1.eq, hρ.isHermitian.eq,
   380	          Matrix.mul_assoc]
   381	      _ = Matrix.trace (T * S * ρ) := by
   382	        exact (Matrix.trace_mul_cycle T S ρ).symm
   383	  have hcross :
   384	      (Matrix.trace (S * T * ρ)).re = (Matrix.trace (T * S * ρ)).re := by
   385	    have := congrArg Complex.re hstar
   386	    simpa [Complex.star_def, Complex.conj_re] using this
   387	  have hdiff :
   388	      (S - T)ᴴ * (S - T) =
   389	        (2 : ℂ) • (1 : Op ι) - S * T - T * S := by
   390	    rw [Matrix.conjTranspose_sub, hS.1.eq, hT.1.eq]
   391	    calc
   392	      (S - T) * (S - T) = S * S - S * T - T * S + T * T := by
   393	        noncomm_ring
   394	      _ = (2 : ℂ) • (1 : Op ι) - S * T - T * S := by
   395	        rw [hS.2, hT.2]
   396	        module
   397	  unfold stateDepDistSq
   398	  rw [hdiff]
   399	  simp only [Matrix.sub_mul, Matrix.trace_sub, Complex.sub_re]
   400	  rw [smul_mul_assoc, one_mul, Matrix.trace_smul, htrace]
   401	  norm_num [Complex.mul_re]
   402	  rw [hcross]
   403	  ring
   404	
   405	/-- The squared binary-measurement distance is one minus the real
   406	state-dependent correlation. -/
   407	theorem binaryObservableDistSq_eq_one_sub_correlation
   408	    {ι : Type} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
   409	    (S T ρ : Op ι) (hS : IsBinaryObservable S)
   410	    (hT : IsBinaryObservable T) (hρ : ρ.PosSemidef)
   411	    (htrace : Matrix.trace ρ = 1) :
   412	    binaryObservableDistSq S T ρ =
   413	      1 - (Matrix.trace (S * T * ρ)).re := by
   414	  rw [binaryObservableDistSq_eq_stateDepDistSq_div_two,
   415	    stateDepDistSq_eq_two_sub_two_mul_correlation S T ρ hS hT hρ htrace]
   416	  ring
   417	
   418	end
   419	
   420	end MIPStarRE.QPBT

     4	/-!
     5	# Binary observables and the state-dependent distance
     6	
     7	This file collects the notions in which the quantum linearity theorem of
     8	Natarajan and Vidick is stated: binary observables, the rank-one density
     9	operator of an ancillary vector, and the squared state-dependent distance
    10	between two operators weighted by a positive semidefinite trace-one operator.
    11	The theorem itself, `exists_exactly_linear_observables`, is stated and proved
    12	in `MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Linearity.lean` from the Boolean Fourier,
    13	operator BLR, Naimark rounding, and representation stability modules under
    14	`MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Linearity/`, all of which build on this file.
    15	
    16	## Main definitions
    17	
    18	* `IsBinaryObservable`: a Hermitian operator whose square is the identity.
    19	* `ancProj`: the rank-one density operator `|v⟩⟨v|` of a vector `v`.
    20	* `stateDepDistSq`: the squared state-dependent distance
    21	  `d_ρ(S, T)^2 = Re Tr((S - T)^† (S - T) ρ)`.
    22	
    23	## References
    24	
    25	The notions are those of `thm:linearity` in
    26	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:104-150`, quoted in the QPBT
    27	paper at `references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:713-725`
    28	from Theorem 10 of Natarajan--Vidick, arXiv:1610.03574,
    29	`references/nv-paper/fullpaper.tex:1074-1088`; the state-dependent distance is
    30	defined there at lines 866--875.
    31	-/
    32	
    33	open scoped BigOperators Matrix MatrixOrder ComplexOrder
    34	
    35	namespace MIPStarRE.QPBT
    36	
    37	open MIPStarRE.LDT
    38	open MIPStarRE.Quantum
    39	
    40	noncomputable section
    41	
    42	/-- A binary observable is a Hermitian operator whose square is the identity.
    43	This is the finite-matrix realization of `Obs(H)` in `thm:linearity`, blueprint
    44	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:104-150`, quoted at paper
    45	`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:713-725`. -/
    46	def IsBinaryObservable {ι : Type} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    47	    (O : Op ι) : Prop :=
    48	  O.IsHermitian ∧ O * O = 1
    49	
    50	/-- The rank-one density operator associated with an ancillary vector.  This
    51	is the state `|anc⟩⟨anc|` of the extension `ρ' = ρ ⊗ |anc⟩⟨anc|` in
    52	`thm:linearity`, blueprint
    53	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:104-150`. -/
    54	noncomputable def ancProj {ι : Type} [Fintype ι]
    55	    (v : EuclideanSpace ℂ ι) : Op ι :=
    56	  let w := (EuclideanSpace.equiv ι ℂ) v
    57	  Matrix.vecMulVec w (star w)
    58	
    59	/-- Squared state-dependent distance between two operators.  This is the
    60	quantity `d_ρ(S,T)^2` in `thm:linearity`, blueprint
    61	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:104-150`, the state-dependent
    62	distance of `references/nv-paper/fullpaper.tex:873-875`. -/
    63	noncomputable def stateDepDistSq {ι : Type} [Fintype ι]
    64	    (S T ρ : Op ι) : ℝ :=
    65	  (Matrix.trace ((S - T)ᴴ * (S - T) * ρ)).re
    66	
    67	end
    68	
    69	end MIPStarRE.QPBT

     4	/-!
     5	# Section 5 — Making measurements projective: definitions
     6	
     7	Definitions for Naimark dilation and orthonormalization, matching
     8	Section 5 of `references/ldt-paper/orthonormalization.tex` and
     9	Chapter 4 of the blueprint (`blueprint/src/chapter/ch04_projective.tex`).
    10	
    11	## Naimark dilation structure
    12	
    13	The key mathematical content is the **Naimark dilation theorem**: given
    14	submeasurements on a bipartite space, there exist auxiliary registers and
    15	projective measurements on the enlarged space that preserve all correlations
    16	exactly.
    17	
    18	### One-measurement Naimark (Lemma 5.2)
    19	
    20	The building block is the one-measurement Naimark lemma. Given a
    21	submeasurement `{M_a}_{a ∈ α}` on `Op d`, it produces a projective
    22	submeasurement on the enlarged space `Op (d × Option α)`. The auxiliary
    23	register has dimension `|α| + 1`, with the extra dimension absorbing the
    24	"missing mass" `I − ∑ M_a`. The construction uses the isometry
    25	`V|ψ⟩ = ∑_a √M_a |ψ⟩ ⊗ |a⟩ + √(I−M)|ψ⟩ ⊗ |⊥⟩` and defines
    26	`P̂_a = V† (I ⊗ |a⟩⟨a|) V`.
    27	
    28	### Questionwise Naimark data
    29	
    30	For a prospective full bipartite assembly, one-measurement Naimark is applied
    31	independently to each question on each side.  The current formal interface
    32	records these questionwise local data and their marginal preservation
    33	identities, not the full tensor-product correlation theorem.
    34	
    35	## Matrix-level witnesses
    36	
    37	Concrete `Matrix d d ℂ` witnesses are provided alongside the abstract
    38	operator-algebra formulation, giving honest probability and overlap formulas.
    39	-/
    40	
    41	open scoped BigOperators MatrixOrder Matrix ComplexOrder
    42	
    43	namespace MIPStarRE.LDT.MakingMeasurementsProjective
    44	
    45	open MIPStarRE.LDT
    46	
    47	/-! ### Finite Hilbert space infrastructure -/
    48	
    49	/-- A finite-dimensional Hilbert space represented by a finite index type. -/
    50	structure FiniteHilbertSpace where
    51	  carrier : Type*
    52	  instFintype : Fintype carrier
    53	  instDecidableEq : DecidableEq carrier
    54	  instNonempty : Nonempty carrier
    55	
    56	attribute [instance] FiniteHilbertSpace.instFintype
    57	attribute [instance] FiniteHilbertSpace.instDecidableEq
    58	attribute [instance] FiniteHilbertSpace.instNonempty
    59	
    60	/-- Concrete operators on a finite Hilbert space. -/
    61	abbrev MatrixOperator (H : FiniteHilbertSpace) :=
    62	  MIPStarRE.Quantum.Op H.carrier
    63

   175	/-! ### One-measurement Naimark dilation (Lemma 5.2)
   176	
   177	The one-measurement Naimark dilation is the building block for the full
   178	theorem. Given a submeasurement `M` on space `d`, it produces a projective
   179	submeasurement on the enlarged space `d × Option α`, where `Option α`
   180	models the auxiliary register with one extra dimension `none = ⊥` for the
   181	missing mass `I − ∑ M_a`. -/
   182	
   183	/-- The auxiliary pure-state projector `|⊥⟩⟨⊥|` on `Option α`, where `⊥ = none`.
   184	This is the initial state of the auxiliary register before the Naimark
   185	isometry is applied. -/
   186	def naimarkAuxProjector (α : Type*) [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α] :
   187	    MIPStarRE.Quantum.Op (Option α) :=
   188	  Matrix.single none none 1
   189	
   190	/-- The lifted density matrix for one-measurement Naimark dilation:
   191	`ρ_lifted = |Option α| · (ρ ⊗ |⊥⟩⟨⊥|)`.
   192	The scaling by `|Option α|` ensures the normalized trace is preserved:
   193	`τ'(ρ_lifted) = τ(ρ)`, where `τ'` is the normalized trace on the enlarged space. -/
   194	noncomputable def oneMeasLiftedDensity {d : Type*} [Fintype d] [DecidableEq d]
   195	    (α : Type*) [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α]
   196	    (ρ : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Op d) :
   197	    MIPStarRE.Quantum.Op (d × Option α) :=
   198	  (Fintype.card (Option α) : ℂ) • Matrix.kronecker ρ (naimarkAuxProjector α)
   199	
   200	/-- One-measurement Naimark dilation data at the matrix level.
   201	
   202	Given a submeasurement `M : Submeasurement α d`, this witnesses the existence
   203	of a projective submeasurement on the enlarged space `d × Option α` that
   204	preserves all expectation values. This is Lemma 5.2 of the paper.
   205	
   206	The construction: let `V : H → H ⊗ ℂ^{|α|+1}` be the isometry
   207	`V|ψ⟩ = ∑_a √M_a |ψ⟩ ⊗ |a⟩ + √(I−M)|ψ⟩ ⊗ |⊥⟩`.
   208	Then `P̂_a = V† (I ⊗ |a⟩⟨a|) V` is a projection, and
   209	`⟨ψ|M_a|ψ⟩ = ⟨ψ⊗⊥|P̂_a|ψ⊗⊥⟩`. -/
   210	structure OneMeasNaimarkData (α : Type*) [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α]
   211	    (d : Type*) [Fintype d] [DecidableEq d] where
   212	  /-- The source submeasurement being dilated. -/
   213	  source : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Submeasurement α d
   214	  /-- The dilated projective effects on `d × Option α`.
   215	  For outcome `some a`, this is the Naimark projector `P̂_a`.
   216	  For outcome `none`, this is the projector for the "missing mass". -/
   217	  liftedEffect : Option α → MIPStarRE.Quantum.Op (d × Option α)
   218	  /-- Each lifted effect is a genuine orthogonal projection. Positivity follows
   219	  from `IsStarProjection.nonneg`. -/
   220	  lifted_isProj : ∀ a, MIPStarRE.Quantum.IsProj (liftedEffect a)
   221	  /-- The lifted projections sum to at most identity (which together with
   222	  `lifted_isProj` implies mutual orthogonality). -/
   223	  lifted_sum_le_one : ∑ a, liftedEffect a ≤ 1
   224	  /-- **Expectation preservation**: for any operator `ρ` on `Op d`,
   225	  the expectation of outcome `a` under the original submeasurement equals
   226	  the expectation under the dilated projective submeasurement with the
   227	  Naimark-lifted state. The identity is linear, so it holds for all operators,
   228	  not just density matrices. This is the core content of the dilation. -/
   229	  expectation_preservation : ∀ (ρ : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Op d) (a : α),
   230	    MIPStarRE.Quantum.normalizedTrace (ρ * source.effect a) =
   231	      MIPStarRE.Quantum.normalizedTrace
   232	        (oneMeasLiftedDensity α ρ * liftedEffect (some a))
   233	
   234	/-- Positivity of a lifted Naimark effect, derived from its projectivity.
   235	
   236	Lean-only consequence of the one-measurement Naimark data: the paper records
   237	the lifted effects as projections, and positivity is supplied here by the
   238	Mathlib star-projection order theorem through `IsStarProjection.nonneg`. -/
   239	theorem OneMeasNaimarkData.lifted_pos {α : Type*} [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α]
   240	    {d : Type*} [Fintype d] [DecidableEq d]
   241	    (data : OneMeasNaimarkData α d) (a : Option α) :
   242	    0 ≤ data.liftedEffect a :=
   243	  (data.lifted_isProj a).nonneg

    18	/-- The Naimark column acts as an isometry on the input subspace: `VP = V`. -/
    19	private lemma oneMeasNaimarkColumn_mul_inputProj
    20	    {α : Type*} [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α]
    21	    {d : Type*} [Fintype d] [DecidableEq d]
    22	    (M : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Submeasurement α d) :
    23	    oneMeasNaimarkColumn M * oneMeasNaimarkInputProj (α := α) (d := d) =
    24	      oneMeasNaimarkColumn M := by
    25	  ext ⟨d₁, oa₁⟩ ⟨d₂, oa₂⟩
    26	  simp only [Matrix.mul_apply, oneMeasNaimarkInputProj,
    27	    oneMeasNaimarkAuxTransition]
    28	  cases oa₂ with
    29	  | none =>
    30	    have : ∀ x : d × Option α,
    31	        oneMeasNaimarkColumn M (d₁, oa₁) x *
    32	          Matrix.kronecker (1 : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Op d)
    33	            (Matrix.single (none : Option α) (none : Option α) (1 : ℂ)) x (d₂, none) =
    34	          if x = (d₂, (none : Option α)) then
    35	            oneMeasNaimarkColumn M (d₁, oa₁) (d₂, none)
    36	          else 0 := by
    37	      intro ⟨k₁, k₂⟩
    38	      cases k₂ with
    39	      | none =>
    40	          by_cases h : k₁ = d₂ <;>
    41	            simp [Matrix.kronecker, Prod.ext_iff, h]
    42	      | some a =>
    43	          have hneq : (k₁, some a) ≠ (d₂, (none : Option α)) := by
    44	            intro h
    45	            cases h
    46	          simp [Matrix.kronecker, hneq]
    47	    simp_rw [this]
    48	    rw [Finset.sum_ite_eq' Finset.univ (d₂, (none : Option α)) (fun _ =>
    49	      oneMeasNaimarkColumn M (d₁, oa₁) (d₂, none))]
    50	    simp
    51	  | some a₂ =>
    52	    simp [oneMeasNaimarkColumn, Matrix.kronecker]

    54	-- This is independent of Naimark and could be moved to `LDT/Preliminaries`.
    55	/-- **Partial isometry to unitary extension** (general fact).
    56	
    57	If `V†V = P` where `P` is a projection and `V = VP`, then there exists
    58	a unitary `U` on the full space with `UP = V`.
    59	
    60	This is a standard result in finite-dimensional linear algebra: V is an
    61	isometry from range(P) to V's range, and in finite dimensions any
    62	isometry between subspaces extends to a unitary.
    63	
    64	**Mathlib route**: `LinearIsometry.extend` provides the extension for
    65	linear isometries between inner product spaces. The gap is the
    66	matrix-to-`EuclideanSpace` transport. -/
    67	private lemma partialIsometry_to_unitary
    68	    {n : Type*} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n]
    69	    (V P : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Op n)
    70	    (hP : MIPStarRE.Quantum.IsProj P)
    71	    (hVP : V * P = V)
    72	    (hVV : Vᴴ * V = P) :
    73	    ∃ U : Matrix.unitaryGroup n ℂ,
    74	      (U : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Op n) * P = V := by
    75	  classical
    76	  have toEuclideanLin_mul :
    77	      ∀ A B : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Op n,
    78	        Matrix.toEuclideanLin (A * B) =
    79	          (Matrix.toEuclideanLin A).comp (Matrix.toEuclideanLin B) := by
    80	    intro A B
    81	    simp [Matrix.toEuclideanLin, Matrix.toLpLin_mul_same (p := (2 : ENNReal)) A B]
    82	  let Pₗ : EuclideanSpace ℂ n →ₗ[ℂ] EuclideanSpace ℂ n := Matrix.toEuclideanLin P
    83	  let Vₗ : EuclideanSpace ℂ n →ₗ[ℂ] EuclideanSpace ℂ n := Matrix.toEuclideanLin V
    84	  let S : Submodule ℂ (EuclideanSpace ℂ n) := LinearMap.range Pₗ
    85	  letI : InnerProductSpace ℂ S := Submodule.innerProductSpace S
    86	  have hP_fix : ∀ x : S, Pₗ (x : EuclideanSpace ℂ n) = x := by
    87	    intro x
    88	    rcases x.2 with ⟨y, hy⟩
    89	    rw [← hy]
    90	    calc
    91	      Pₗ (Pₗ y) = (Pₗ.comp Pₗ) y := rfl
    92	      _ = Matrix.toEuclideanLin (P * P) y := by rw [toEuclideanLin_mul]
    93	      _ = Pₗ y := by rw [hP.isIdempotentElem.eq]
    94	  have hVP_lin : Vₗ.comp Pₗ = Vₗ := by
    95	    calc
    96	      Vₗ.comp Pₗ = Matrix.toEuclideanLin (V * P) := by rw [toEuclideanLin_mul]
    97	      _ = Vₗ := by rw [hVP]
    98	  have hgram : Matrix.toEuclideanLin (Vᴴ * V) = Pₗ := by
    99	    calc
   100	      Matrix.toEuclideanLin (Vᴴ * V) = Matrix.toEuclideanLin P := by rw [hVV]
   101	      _ = Pₗ := rfl
   102	  let Llin : S →ₗ[ℂ] EuclideanSpace ℂ n := Vₗ.comp S.subtype
   103	  have hLnorm : ∀ x : S, ‖Llin x‖ = ‖x‖ := by
   104	    exact (LinearMap.norm_map_iff_inner_map_map
   105	      (𝕜 := ℂ) (E := S) (E' := EuclideanSpace ℂ n)
   106	      (F := S →ₗ[ℂ] EuclideanSpace ℂ n) Llin).2 fun x y => by
   107	      have hy : Matrix.toEuclideanLin (Vᴴ * V) (y : EuclideanSpace ℂ n) = y := by
   108	        calc
   109	          Matrix.toEuclideanLin (Vᴴ * V) (y : EuclideanSpace ℂ n) =
   110	              Pₗ (y : EuclideanSpace ℂ n) := by rw [hgram]
   111	          _ = y := hP_fix y
   112	      calc
   113	        inner ℂ (Llin x) (Llin y) =
   114	            inner ℂ (Vₗ (x : EuclideanSpace ℂ n)) (Vₗ (y : EuclideanSpace ℂ n)) := rfl
   115	        _ = inner ℂ (x : EuclideanSpace ℂ n)
   116	            (Matrix.toEuclideanLin (Vᴴ * V) (y : EuclideanSpace ℂ n)) := by
   117	          dsimp [Vₗ]
   118	          rw [Matrix.toEuclideanLin_conjTranspose_mul_self]
   119	          exact (LinearMap.adjoint_inner_right (𝕜 := ℂ)
   120	            (Matrix.toEuclideanLin V) (x : EuclideanSpace ℂ n)
   121	            (Matrix.toEuclideanLin V (y : EuclideanSpace ℂ n))).symm
   122	        _ = inner ℂ (x : EuclideanSpace ℂ n) (y : EuclideanSpace ℂ n) := by rw [hy]
   123	        _ = inner ℂ x y := rfl
   124	  let L : S →ₗᵢ[ℂ] EuclideanSpace ℂ n := { toLinearMap := Llin, norm_map' := hLnorm }
   125	  let Ulin : EuclideanSpace ℂ n →ₗᵢ[ℂ] EuclideanSpace ℂ n :=
   126	    LinearIsometry.extend (𝕜 := ℂ) (V := EuclideanSpace ℂ n) (S := S) L
   127	  let Umat : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Op n :=
   128	    Matrix.toEuclideanLin.symm Ulin.toLinearMap
   129	  have hUmat_lin : Matrix.toEuclideanLin Umat = Ulin.toLinearMap := by
   130	    exact Matrix.toEuclideanLin.apply_symm_apply Ulin.toLinearMap
   131	  have hUstarU : Umatᴴ * Umat = 1 := by
   132	    apply Matrix.toEuclideanLin.injective
   133	    calc
   134	      Matrix.toEuclideanLin (Umatᴴ * Umat) =
   135	          (Matrix.toEuclideanLin Umat).adjoint.comp (Matrix.toEuclideanLin Umat) := by
   136	            rw [Matrix.toEuclideanLin_conjTranspose_mul_self]
   137	      _ = Ulin.toLinearMap.adjoint.comp Ulin.toLinearMap := by rw [hUmat_lin]
   138	      _ = 1 := by exact Ulin.adjoint_comp_self'
   139	      _ = Matrix.toEuclideanLin (1 : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Op n) := by
   140	            rw [Matrix.toEuclideanLin, Matrix.toLpLin_one]
   141	            rfl
   142	  let U : Matrix.unitaryGroup n ℂ := ⟨Umat, (Matrix.mem_unitaryGroup_iff').2 hUstarU⟩
   143	  refine ⟨U, ?_⟩
   144	  apply Matrix.toEuclideanLin.injective
   145	  apply LinearMap.ext
   146	  intro x
   147	  have hExt : Ulin (Pₗ x) = Vₗ (Pₗ x) := by
   148	    simpa [Ulin, L, Llin] using
   149	      (LinearIsometry.extend_apply L ⟨Pₗ x, LinearMap.mem_range_self Pₗ x⟩)
   150	  calc
   151	    Matrix.toEuclideanLin ((U : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Op n) * P) x =
   152	        Matrix.toEuclideanLin Umat (Pₗ x) := by
   153	          rw [toEuclideanLin_mul]
   154	          rfl
   155	    _ = Ulin (Pₗ x) := by
   156	          rw [hUmat_lin]
   157	          rfl
   158	    _ = Vₗ (Pₗ x) := hExt
   159	    _ = Vₗ x := by
   160	          have hx := congrArg
   161	            (fun f : EuclideanSpace ℂ n →ₗ[ℂ] EuclideanSpace ℂ n => f x) hVP_lin
   162	          simpa [LinearMap.comp_apply] using hx
   163	    _ = Matrix.toEuclideanLin V x := rfl

   165	private lemma normalizedTrace_oneMeasLiftedDensity_mul_auxProj
   166	    {α : Type*} [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α]
   167	    {d : Type*} [Fintype d] [DecidableEq d]
   168	    (ρ X : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Op d) :
   169	    MIPStarRE.Quantum.normalizedTrace
   170	      (oneMeasLiftedDensity α ρ * Matrix.kronecker X (naimarkAuxProjector α)) =
   171	        MIPStarRE.Quantum.normalizedTrace (ρ * X) := by
   172	  unfold oneMeasLiftedDensity
   173	  rw [smul_mul_assoc, MIPStarRE.Quantum.normalizedTrace_smul]
   174	  unfold MIPStarRE.Quantum.normalizedTrace naimarkAuxProjector
   175	  have hmul :
   176	      Matrix.kronecker ρ
   177	          (Matrix.single none none (1 : ℂ) : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Op (Option α)) *
   178	          Matrix.kronecker X
   179	            (Matrix.single none none (1 : ℂ) : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Op (Option α)) =
   180	        Matrix.kronecker (ρ * X)
   181	          ((Matrix.single none none (1 : ℂ) : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Op (Option α)) *
   182	            (Matrix.single none none (1 : ℂ) : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Op (Option α))) := by
   183	    simpa using
   184	      (Matrix.mul_kronecker_mul ρ X
   185	        (Matrix.single none none (1 : ℂ) : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Op (Option α))
   186	        (Matrix.single none none (1 : ℂ) : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Op (Option α))).symm
   187	  rw [hmul]
   188	  have htrace :
   189	      ((ρ * X).kronecker
   190	          ((Matrix.single none none (1 : ℂ) : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Op (Option α)) *
   191	            (Matrix.single none none (1 : ℂ) : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Op (Option α)))).trace =
   192	        (ρ * X).trace *
   193	          ((Matrix.single none none (1 : ℂ) : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Op (Option α)) *
   194	            (Matrix.single none none (1 : ℂ) : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Op (Option α))).trace := by
   195	    simpa using
   196	      Matrix.trace_kronecker (ρ * X)
   197	        ((Matrix.single none none (1 : ℂ) : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Op (Option α)) *
   198	          (Matrix.single none none (1 : ℂ) : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Op (Option α)))
   199	  rw [htrace]
   200	  have hauxTrace :
   201	      ((Matrix.single none none (1 : ℂ) : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Op (Option α)) *
   202	        (Matrix.single none none (1 : ℂ) : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Op (Option α))).trace = 1 := by
   203	    simp
   204	  rw [hauxTrace]

   218	
   219	For any submeasurement `M : Submeasurement α d`, there exists a projective
   220	submeasurement on the enlarged space `d × Option α` such that for every
   221	operator `ρ` on `Op d` and outcome `a`:
   222	`τ(ρ · M_a) = τ'(ρ_lifted · P̂_a)`
   223	where `ρ_lifted = |Option α| · (ρ ⊗ |⊥⟩⟨⊥|)` and `P̂_a` is the
   224	dilated projector.
   225	
   226	**Proof sketch**: Let `V|ψ⟩ = ∑_a √M_a|ψ⟩ ⊗ |a⟩ + √(I−M)|ψ⟩ ⊗ |⊥⟩`.

   228	Define `P̂_a = V†(I ⊗ |a⟩⟨a|)V`. Then `P̂_a` is an orthogonal projection
   229	(since `|a⟩⟨a|` is), and the compression identity
   230	`(I⊗⟨⊥|) P̂_a (I⊗|⊥⟩) = √M_a · √M_a = M_a` gives the result.

     6	This file completes the proof of the quantum linearity theorem of Natarajan

    13	
    14	The extension, the ancillary vector, and the exactly linear family are those
    15	of the Naimark rounding of the Fourier-square POVM.  The main computation is
    16	an identity, not an inequality: the average squared state-dependent operator
    17	distance between the rounded family and the ampliated original family,
    18	weighted by `ρ ⊗ |anc⟩⟨anc|`, equals the average multiplicative defect of the
    19	original family weighted by `ρ`.  Both sides equal
    20	`2 - 2 * (two-query correlation)`.  The left side reduces to the
    21	correlation by compressing the rounded observables along the ancillary vector
    22	and applying the cubic Fourier identity; the right side is the operator BLR
    23	computation, including the reindexing of the uniform pair.  No commutation
    24	among the observables is assumed, and the weight `ρ` is never replaced by the
    25	normalized trace.
    26	
    27	## Main results
    28	
    29	* `heteroKron_ancProj_posSemidef` and `trace_heteroKron_ancProj`: the extended
    30	  weight `ρ ⊗ |anc⟩⟨anc|` is again positive semidefinite with trace one.
    31	* `re_trace_roundedObservable_mul_heteroKron`: the compression of the
    32	  correlation between a rounded observable and the ampliated original
    33	  observable to the original space.
    34	* `stateDepDistSq_roundedObservable`: the pointwise distance between a rounded
    35	  observable and the ampliated original observable, in terms of the overlap
    36	  with the character sum of the Fourier-square POVM.
    37	* `avg_stateDepDistSq_roundedObservable_eq_avg_multiplicativeDefect`: the
    38	  distance/defect identity
    39	  `E_u d_{ρ'}(L^u, O^u ⊗ 1)^2 = E_{u,v} d_ρ(O^u O^v, O^{u+v})^2`.
    40	* `exists_exact_boolean_representation`: the Boolean representation stability
    41	  theorem, obtained by weakening the identity to the incoming bound.
    42	
    43	## References
    44	
    45	Natarajan--Vidick, arXiv:1610.03574, Theorem 10 and its Fourier/Naimark
    46	proof, `references/nv-paper/fullpaper.tex:1074-1113`; the closing step, which
    47	converts the overlap certificate into the distance bound, is at lines
    48	1104--1112, and the state-dependent distance is defined at lines 866--900.
    49	The QPBT paper quotes the theorem at
    50	`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:711-725`.  The
    51	blueprint statement is `thm:linearity` in
    52	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:98-147`, and the
    53	correlation-form statement is `exists_exactly_linear_observables` in
    54	`MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Linearity.lean`.  The declarations of this file are
    55	collected in the blueprint as `lem:boolean-representation-stability`.  The
    56	normalization convention, under which the incoming average multiplicative
    57	defect and the outgoing average squared state-dependent operator distance
    58	carry the same constant, is recorded in
    59	`docs/paper-gaps/qpbt_linearity-distance-normalization.tex`.
    60	-/

    76	theorem ancProj_posSemidef {ι : Type} [Fintype ι] (v : EuclideanSpace ℂ ι) :

   137	theorem re_trace_roundedObservable_mul_heteroKron {t : ℕ} {ι : Type}

   142	        heteroKron (O u) (1 : Op (Option (Fin t → ZMod 2))) *
   143	        heteroKron ρ (ancProj (naimarkAncilla t)))).re =

   147	  have hT := (isBinaryObservable_heteroKron_one (ι' := Option (Fin t → ZMod 2)) (hO u)).1

   153	    unfold heteroKron
   154	    simp only [Matrix.kronecker]
   155	    rw [← Matrix.mul_kronecker_mul, Matrix.mul_one]
   156	  have hstar :
   157	      star (Matrix.trace (roundedObservable O hO u *
   158	          heteroKron (O u) (1 : Op (Option (Fin t → ZMod 2))) *
   159	          heteroKron ρ (ancProj (naimarkAncilla t)))) =

   163	      star (Matrix.trace (roundedObservable O hO u *
   164	          heteroKron (O u) (1 : Op (Option (Fin t → ZMod 2))) *
   165	          heteroKron ρ (ancProj (naimarkAncilla t)))) =

   167	            heteroKron (O u) (1 : Op (Option (Fin t → ZMod 2))) *
   168	            heteroKron ρ (ancProj (naimarkAncilla t)))ᴴ) := by

   173	        simp only [Matrix.conjTranspose_mul, hL.eq, hT.eq, hρ'.eq, Matrix.mul_assoc]

   183	  have := congrArg Complex.re hstar
   184	  simpa [Complex.star_def, Complex.conj_re] using this

   186	/-- The squared state-dependent distance between a rounded observable `L^u` and

   193	`docs/paper-gaps/qpbt_linearity-distance-normalization.tex`. -/
   194	theorem stateDepDistSq_roundedObservable {t : ℕ} {ι : Type}
   195	    [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
   196	    (O : (Fin t → ZMod 2) → Op ι) (hO : ∀ a, IsBinaryObservable (O a))

   201	      2 - 2 * (Matrix.trace (O u * (∑ v : Fin t → ZMod 2, booleanCharacter v u •

   203	  rw [stateDepDistSq_eq_two_sub_two_mul_correlation _ _ _

   232	    avg_overlap_fourierSquare_eq_sum_cube, operatorFourier_cube_trace_eq_correlation,
   233	    avg_multiplicativeDefect_eq_two_sub_two_mul_correlation O hO ρ hρ htrace]

   235	/-! ## Boolean representation stability -/
   236	
   237	/-- Boolean representation stability.  Let `t` be positive, `η ≥ 0`, `ρ` a
   238	positive semidefinite trace-one operator on a finite carrier, and `O^u`, for
   239	`u ∈ F_2^t`, binary observables whose products satisfy
   240	`E_{u,v} d_ρ(O^u O^v, O^{u+v})^2 ≤ η`.  Then there are a finite ancillary
   241	carrier, a unit vector `anc` in it, and binary observables `L^u` on the
   242	product carrier with `L^u L^v = L^{u+v}` for all `u, v` and
   243	`E_u d_{ρ'}(L^u, O^u ⊗ 1)^2 ≤ η`, where `ρ' = ρ ⊗ |anc⟩⟨anc|`.
   244	
   245	The ancillary carrier is `Option (F_2^t)`, the vector is the canonical
   246	ancillary vector of the Naimark dilation, and the family is the rounded
   247	observables of the Fourier-square POVM; the bound is the distance/defect
   248	identity `avg_stateDepDistSq_roundedObservable_eq_avg_multiplicativeDefect`
   249	weakened by the hypothesis.
   250	
   251	**Local fix:** This is the mathematical content of Theorem 10 of
   252	Natarajan--Vidick, `references/nv-paper/fullpaper.tex:1074-1088`, quoted at
   253	`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:711-725` and
   254	stated as `thm:linearity` in
   255	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:98-147`, but not that displayed
   256	statement: the hypothesis here is the average multiplicative defect rather
   257	than the two-query correlation.  By
   258	`avg_multiplicativeDefect_le_two_mul_error`, a correlation at least `1 - δ`
   259	gives the present hypothesis with `η = 2δ`, so the conclusion obtained from a
   260	correlation hypothesis is the bound `2δ` for the average squared
   261	state-dependent operator distance, whereas `thm:linearity` displays the bound
   262	`δ`.  That factor of two is the normalization refuted in
   263	`docs/paper-gaps/qpbt_linearity-distance-normalization.tex`; the blueprint
   264	entry for the present statement is `lem:boolean-representation-stability`.
   265	The positivity of `t` and the nonnegativity of `η` are part of the quoted
   266	statement and are not needed by the proof. -/
   267	theorem exists_exact_boolean_representation {ι : Type}
   268	    [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
   269	    (t : ℕ) (_ht : 0 < t) (η : ℝ) (_hη : 0 ≤ η)
   270	    (ρ : Op ι) (hρ : ρ.PosSemidef) (htrace : ρ.trace = 1)
   271	    (O : (Fin t → ZMod 2) → Op ι)
   272	    (hO : ∀ u, IsBinaryObservable (O u))
   273	    (hdefect :
   274	      avgOver (uniformDistribution ((Fin t → ZMod 2) × (Fin t → ZMod 2)))
   275	        (fun pair => stateDepDistSq (O pair.1 * O pair.2) (O (pair.1 + pair.2)) ρ) ≤ η) :
   276	    ∃ (ι' : Type) (_ : Fintype ι') (_ : DecidableEq ι')
   277	        (anc : EuclideanSpace ℂ ι'),
   278	      ‖anc‖ = 1 ∧
   279	        ∃ L : (Fin t → ZMod 2) → Op (ι × ι'),
   280	          (∀ u, IsBinaryObservable (L u)) ∧
   281	          (∀ u v, L u * L v = L (u + v)) ∧
   282	          avgOver (uniformDistribution (Fin t → ZMod 2))
   283	              (fun u => stateDepDistSq (L u)
   284	                (heteroKron (O u) (1 : Op ι'))
   285	                (heteroKron ρ (ancProj anc))) ≤ η := by
   286	  refine ⟨Option (Fin t → ZMod 2), inferInstance, inferInstance, naimarkAncilla t,
   287	    norm_naimarkAncilla t, roundedObservable O hO, roundedObservable_isBinaryObservable O hO,
   288	    roundedObservable_mul O hO, ?_⟩
   289	  rw [avg_stateDepDistSq_roundedObservable_eq_avg_multiplicativeDefect O hO ρ hρ htrace]

     3	/-!
     4	# Normalized trace, projectors, and spectral truncation
     5	
     6	This module contains the normalized trace `τ`, the squared `τ`-norm, the
     7	paper-facing orthogonal-projection name, and the spectral-truncation witness used
     8	in the low individual degree test formalization.
     9	-/
    10	
    11	open scoped BigOperators MatrixOrder Matrix ComplexOrder Matrix.Norms.Elementwise
    12	open WithLp
    13	
    14	namespace MIPStarRE.Quantum
    15	
    16	variable {d : Type*} [Fintype d]
    17	
    18	/-! ### Normalized trace -/
    19	
    20	/-- The normalized trace `τ(A) = tr(A) / |d|`. -/
    21	noncomputable def normalizedTrace (A : Op d) : ℂ :=
    22	  A.trace / (Fintype.card d : ℂ)
    23	
    24	/-- The normalized trace of the zero operator is zero. -/
    25	@[simp] theorem normalizedTrace_zero : normalizedTrace (0 : Op d) = 0 := by
    26	  simp [normalizedTrace]
    27	
    28	/-- The normalized trace of the identity operator is one. -/
    29	@[simp] theorem normalizedTrace_one [DecidableEq d] [Nonempty d] :
    30	    normalizedTrace (1 : Op d) = 1 := by
    31	  unfold normalizedTrace
    32	  rw [Matrix.trace_one]
    33	  exact div_self (Nat.cast_ne_zero.mpr Fintype.card_ne_zero)
    34	
    35	/-- The normalized trace is additive. -/
    36	theorem normalizedTrace_add (A B : Op d) :
    37	    normalizedTrace (A + B) = normalizedTrace A + normalizedTrace B := by
    38	  simp [normalizedTrace, Matrix.trace_add, add_div]
    39	
    40	/-- The normalized trace sends subtraction to subtraction. -/
    41	theorem normalizedTrace_sub (A B : Op d) :
    42	    normalizedTrace (A - B) = normalizedTrace A - normalizedTrace B := by
    43	  simp [normalizedTrace, Matrix.trace_sub, sub_div]
    44	
    45	/-- Scalar multiplication pulls out of the normalized trace. -/
    46	theorem normalizedTrace_smul (c : ℂ) (A : Op d) :
    47	    normalizedTrace (c • A) = c * normalizedTrace A := by
    48	  simp [normalizedTrace, Matrix.trace_smul]
    49	  ring
    50	
    51	/-- The normalized trace is invariant under swapping two multiplicative factors. -/
    52	theorem normalizedTrace_mul_comm (A B : Op d) :
    53	    normalizedTrace (A * B) = normalizedTrace (B * A) := by
    54	  simp only [normalizedTrace]
    55	  rw [Matrix.trace_mul_comm]
    56	
    57	/-- Simultaneous reindexing of rows and columns preserves the normalized trace. -/
    58	theorem normalizedTrace_reindex {d₁ d₂ : Type*} [Fintype d₁] [Fintype d₂]
    59	    (e : d₁ ≃ d₂) (A : Op d₁) :
    60	    normalizedTrace (Matrix.reindex e e A) = normalizedTrace A := by
    61	  have hcard : Fintype.card d₂ = Fintype.card d₁ := Fintype.card_congr e.symm
    62	  unfold normalizedTrace
    63	  rw [Matrix.trace_reindex]
    64	  simp [hcard]
    65	
    66	/-! ### Squared τ-norm -/
    67	
    68	/--
    69	The squared τ-norm: `‖A‖²_τ = τ(A⋆ A)`.
    70	In finite dimensions this is `(1/d) ∑ᵢⱼ |Aᵢⱼ|²`, the normalized squared
    71	Frobenius norm.
    72	-/
    73	noncomputable def tauNormSq (A : Op d) : ℂ :=
    74	  normalizedTrace (Aᴴ * A)
    75	
    76	/-- The squared τ-norm of the zero operator is zero. -/
    77	@[simp] theorem tauNormSq_zero : tauNormSq (0 : Op d) = 0 := by
    78	  simp [tauNormSq]
    79	
    80	/-! ### Projector predicate -/
    81	
    82	/-- Paper-facing name for Mathlib's predicate that a matrix is a self-adjoint idempotent. -/
    83	abbrev IsProj (P : Op d) : Prop := IsStarProjection P
    84	
    85	/-! ### Spectral truncation -/
    86	
    87	/--
    88	A spectral truncation witness records the passage from a Hermitian matrix `source`
    89	to a projection `target` by truncating the spectrum to `{0, 1}`: eigenvalues
    90	above `1 / 2` are rounded to `1`, and those below are rounded to `0`.
    91	
    92	The key output is the τ-distance bound between `source` and `target`.
    93	-/
    94	structure SpectralTruncation (source target : Op d) : Prop where
    95	  /-- The source matrix is Hermitian. -/
    96	  sourceHermitian : source.IsHermitian
    97	  /-- The target matrix is an orthogonal projection. -/
    98	  targetProj : IsProj target
    99	  /-- Spectral truncation does not increase the defect measured by `tauNormSq`. -/
   100	  tauDistanceBound : Complex.re (tauNormSq (source - target)) ≤

    33	
    34	/-- Averaging the zero function gives zero. -/
    35	theorem avgOver_zero {α : Type*} (𝒟 : Distribution α) :
    36	    avgOver 𝒟 (fun _ => 0) = 0 := by
    37	  simp [Distribution.avgOver_eq_weightedSumLinearMap]
    38	
    39	/-- Averaging preserves order when weights are nonneg. -/
    40	theorem avgOver_mono {α : Type*} (𝒟 : Distribution α) (f g : α → Error)
    41	    (hfg : ∀ a, f a ≤ g a) :
    42	    avgOver 𝒟 f ≤ avgOver 𝒟 g := by
    43	  simp only [avgOver]
    44	  exact Finset.sum_le_sum fun a _ => mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left (hfg a) (𝒟.nonnegative a)
    45	
    46	/-- Averaging a nonneg function with nonneg weights gives a nonneg result. -/
    47	theorem avgOver_nonneg {α : Type*} (𝒟 : Distribution α) (f : α → Error)
    48	    (hf : ∀ a, 0 ≤ f a) :
    49	    0 ≤ avgOver 𝒟 f := by
    50	  simpa [avgOver_zero] using avgOver_mono 𝒟 (fun _ => 0) f hf
    51	
    52	/-- Averaging distributes over addition. -/
    53	theorem avgOver_add {α : Type*} (𝒟 : Distribution α) (f g : α → Error) :
    54	    avgOver 𝒟 (fun a => f a + g a) =
    55	      avgOver 𝒟 f + avgOver 𝒟 g := by
    56	  change avgOver 𝒟 (f + g) = avgOver 𝒟 f + avgOver 𝒟 g
    57	  simpa [Distribution.avgOver_eq_weightedSumLinearMap] using
    58	    map_add (𝒟.weightedSumLinearMap Error) f g
    59	
    60	/-- Averaging distributes over subtraction. -/
    61	theorem avgOver_sub {α : Type*} (𝒟 : Distribution α) (f g : α → Error) :
    62	    avgOver 𝒟 (fun a => f a - g a) =
    63	      avgOver 𝒟 f - avgOver 𝒟 g := by
    64	  change avgOver 𝒟 (f - g) = avgOver 𝒟 f - avgOver 𝒟 g
    65	  simpa [Distribution.avgOver_eq_weightedSumLinearMap] using
    66	    map_sub (𝒟.weightedSumLinearMap Error) f g
    67	
    68	/-- Averaging commutes with scalar multiplication. -/
    69	theorem avgOver_const_mul {α : Type*} (𝒟 : Distribution α)
    70	    (c : Error) (f : α → Error) :
    71	    avgOver 𝒟 (fun a => c * f a) =
    72	      c * avgOver 𝒟 f := by
    73	  change avgOver 𝒟 (c • f) = c • avgOver 𝒟 f
    74	  simp [Distribution.avgOver_eq_weightedSumLinearMap, smul_eq_mul]
    75	
    76	/-- Averaging commutes with scalar multiplication on the right. -/
    77	theorem avgOver_mul_const {α : Type*} (𝒟 : Distribution α)
    78	    (f : α → Error) (c : Error) :
    79	    avgOver 𝒟 (fun a => f a * c) = avgOver 𝒟 f * c := by
    80	  unfold avgOver
    81	  calc
    82	    ∑ a ∈ 𝒟.support, 𝒟.weight a * (f a * c)
    83	      = ∑ a ∈ 𝒟.support, (𝒟.weight a * f a) * c := by
    84	          refine Finset.sum_congr rfl ?_
    85	          intro a _
    86	          ring
    87	    _ = (∑ a ∈ 𝒟.support, 𝒟.weight a * f a) * c := by

    90	/-- Pull a finite outcome sum through an average. -/
    91	theorem avgOver_sum {α β : Type*} [Fintype β]

    93	    avgOver 𝒟 (fun a => ∑ b : β, f a b) =
    94	      ∑ b : β, avgOver 𝒟 (fun a => f a b) := by
    95	  rw [show (fun a => ∑ b : β, f a b) = ∑ b : β, fun a => f a b by

   105	  rw [show (fun a => ∑ b ∈ s, f a b) = ∑ b ∈ s, fun a => f a b by

   116	  simp_rw [Finset.mul_sum]
   117	  rw [Finset.sum_comm]
   118	  refine Finset.sum_congr rfl ?_

   161	/-- A scalar average against a sub-probability distribution is bounded by any

   163	theorem avgOver_le_of_weight_sum_le_one {α : Type*} (𝒟 : Distribution α)

   257	/-- For two probability distributions, total variation is the total positive
   258	part of the signed weight difference `ν - μ`.
   259	
   260	This is the finite-distribution identity
   261	`(1 / 2) * ∑ |μ(a)-ν(a)| = ∑ max 0 (ν(a)-μ(a))`, written for the
   262	project `Distribution` representation. -/
   263	theorem totalVariationDistance_eq_sum_max_sub {α : Type*} [DecidableEq α]
   264	    (μ ν : Distribution α) (hμ : μ.IsProbability) (hν : ν.IsProbability) :
   265	    totalVariationDistance μ ν =
   266	      ∑ a ∈ μ.support ∪ ν.support, max 0 (ν.weight a - μ.weight a) := by
   267	  classical
   268	  let u : Finset α := μ.support ∪ ν.support
   269	  have hμ_union :
   270	      ∑ a ∈ u, μ.weight a = 1 := by
   271	    apply hμ.weight_sum_eq_one_of_subset
   272	    intro a ha
   273	    exact Finset.mem_union_left ν.support ha
   274	  have hν_union :
   275	      ∑ a ∈ u, ν.weight a = 1 := by
   276	    apply hν.weight_sum_eq_one_of_subset
   277	    intro a ha
   278	    exact Finset.mem_union_right μ.support ha
   279	  have hdiff_sum :
   280	      ∑ a ∈ u, (ν.weight a - μ.weight a) = 0 := by
   281	    rw [Finset.sum_sub_distrib, hν_union, hμ_union, sub_self]
   282	  have hmax_abs :
   283	      ∀ a, max 0 (ν.weight a - μ.weight a) =
   284	        ((ν.weight a - μ.weight a) + |μ.weight a - ν.weight a|) / 2 := by
   285	    intro a
   286	    by_cases hle : ν.weight a - μ.weight a ≤ 0
   287	    · have hmax : max 0 (ν.weight a - μ.weight a) = 0 := max_eq_left hle
   288	      have habs : |μ.weight a - ν.weight a| = μ.weight a - ν.weight a := by
   289	        rw [abs_of_nonneg]
   290	        linarith
   291	      rw [hmax, habs]
   292	      ring
   293	    · have hnonneg : 0 ≤ ν.weight a - μ.weight a := le_of_not_ge hle
   294	      have hmax : max 0 (ν.weight a - μ.weight a) =
   295	          ν.weight a - μ.weight a := max_eq_right hnonneg
   296	      have habs : |μ.weight a - ν.weight a| = ν.weight a - μ.weight a := by
   297	        have hμν : μ.weight a ≤ ν.weight a := by linarith
   298	        rw [abs_of_nonpos (sub_nonpos.mpr hμν)]
   299	        ring
   300	      rw [hmax, habs]
   301	      ring
   302	  calc
   303	    totalVariationDistance μ ν
   304	        = (1 / 2) * ∑ a ∈ u, |μ.weight a - ν.weight a| := by
   305	            rfl
   306	    _ = (∑ a ∈ u, (ν.weight a - μ.weight a) +
   307	          ∑ a ∈ u, |μ.weight a - ν.weight a|) / 2 := by
   308	            rw [hdiff_sum]
   309	            ring
   310	    _ = (∑ a ∈ u,
   311	          ((ν.weight a - μ.weight a) + |μ.weight a - ν.weight a|)) / 2 := by
   312	            rw [Finset.sum_add_distrib]
   313	    _ = ∑ a ∈ u,
   314	          ((ν.weight a - μ.weight a) + |μ.weight a - ν.weight a|) / 2 := by
   315	            rw [Finset.sum_div]
   316	    _ = ∑ a ∈ u, max 0 (ν.weight a - μ.weight a) := by
   317	            exact Finset.sum_congr rfl fun a _ => (hmax_abs a).symm

     4	/-!
     5	# Naimark rounding of the Fourier-square POVM
     6	
     7	This file carries out the dilation step in the proof of the quantum linearity
     8	theorem of Natarajan and Vidick.  The Fourier-square POVM `B^u = (hat O^u)^2`
     9	of a family of binary observables `O^a`, indexed by the Boolean cube `F_2^t`,
    10	is dilated by the one-measurement Naimark construction of the low individual
    11	degree test to a projective measurement `{C^u}` on the enlarged space
    12	`ι × Option (F_2^t)`, whose compression along the canonical ancillary vector is
    13	again `{B^u}`.  The signed character sums `L^a = ∑_u (-1)^{u·a} C^u` are then
    14	binary observables satisfying the exact linearity `L^a L^b = L^{a+b}`.
    15	
    16	The one-measurement Naimark construction produces projectors indexed by
    17	`Option (F_2^t)`: one for each Fourier outcome and one for the residual outcome
    18	`none`.  Discarding the residual projector would destroy the resolution of the
    19	identity on the enlarged space, and with it the multiplicativity of the signed
    20	sums.  It is therefore folded into the zero Fourier outcome: the projector
    21	attached to `u = 0` is the complement of the sum of the projectors attached to
    22	the nonzero outcomes.  Since the Fourier-square effects themselves sum to the
    23	identity, the folded projector still compresses to `B^0`.
    24	
    25	## Main definitions and results
    26	
    27	* `naimarkAncilla`, `norm_naimarkAncilla`, `ancProj_naimarkAncilla`: the
    28	  canonical ancillary unit vector and its rank-one density.
    29	* `roundedFourierPVM` with `roundedFourierPVM_isProj`,
    30	  `roundedFourierPVM_sum_eq_one`, `roundedFourierPVM_mul_eq_zero_of_ne`, and
    31	  `trace_heteroKron_mul_roundedFourierPVM`: the dilated projective measurement
    32	  and its compression to the Fourier-square POVM.
    33	* `roundedObservable` with `roundedObservable_mul` and
    34	  `roundedObservable_isBinaryObservable`: the exactly linear binary observables.
    35	* `trace_heteroKron_mul_roundedObservable`: the compression of the rounded
    36	  observables, whose identity yields the averaged distance bound.
    37	
    38	## References
    39	
    40	Natarajan--Vidick, arXiv:1610.03574, proof of Theorem 10,
    41	`references/nv-paper/fullpaper.tex:1095-1104`: the Naimark dilation of `{B^u}`
    42	is at lines 1099--1100, the observables `𝒜(a) = ∑_u (-1)^{u·a} C^u` at lines
    43	1100--1102, and their exact linearity at lines 1103--1104.  The QPBT paper
    44	quotes the theorem at
    45	`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:711-725`, and
    46	the blueprint statement is `thm:linearity` in
    47	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:98-133`.  The one-measurement
    48	Naimark construction reused here is `oneMeasNaimark` in
    49	`MIPStarRE/LDT/MakingMeasurementsProjective/NaimarkOneMeas.lean`, with its data
    50	structure in `MIPStarRE/LDT/MakingMeasurementsProjective/Defs.lean`.
    51	-/

    63	/-! ## The canonical ancillary vector -/
    64	
    65	/-- The canonical ancillary vector of the Naimark dilation: the basis vector of
    66	the residual index `none` in `Option (F_2^t)`.  This is the pure state `|anc⟩`
    67	of `references/nv-paper/fullpaper.tex:1099-1100`; in the one-measurement
    68	Naimark construction it is the initial state `|⊥⟩` of the auxiliary register. -/
    69	def naimarkAncilla (t : ℕ) : EuclideanSpace ℂ (Option (Fin t → ZMod 2)) :=

    71	
    72	/-- The canonical ancillary vector is a unit vector. -/

    76	/-- The rank-one density `|anc⟩⟨anc|` of the canonical ancillary vector is the
