    78	theorem ancProj_naimarkAncilla (t : ℕ) :
    79	    ancProj (naimarkAncilla t) = naimarkAuxProjector (Fin t → ZMod 2) := by
    80	  ext i j
    81	  cases i <;> cases j <;>
    82	    simp [ancProj, naimarkAncilla, naimarkAuxProjector, Matrix.vecMulVec_apply]
    83	
    84	/-! ## The Naimark dilation of the Fourier-square POVM -/
    85	
    86	/-- The one-measurement Naimark dilation data of the Fourier-square POVM
    87	`{B^u}`, supplied by `oneMeasNaimark`: a family of projectors on
    88	`ι × Option (F_2^t)`, indexed by `Option (F_2^t)`, summing to at most the
    89	identity and reproducing every expectation value of `{B^u}` in the lifted
    90	state.  This is the projective measurement produced by Naimark's theorem at
    91	`references/nv-paper/fullpaper.tex:1099-1100`, before the residual outcome is
    92	folded into the zero outcome. -/
    93	def fourierNaimarkData {t : ℕ} {ι : Type} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    94	    (O : (Fin t → ZMod 2) → Op ι) (hO : ∀ a, IsBinaryObservable (O a)) :
    95	    OneMeasNaimarkData (Fin t → ZMod 2) ι :=
    96	  Classical.choose (oneMeasNaimark (fourierSquareMeasurement O hO).toSubmeasurement)
    97	
    98	/-- The Naimark dilation data of `fourierNaimarkData` dilates the Fourier-square
    99	POVM. -/
   100	theorem fourierNaimarkData_source {t : ℕ} {ι : Type} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
   101	    (O : (Fin t → ZMod 2) → Op ι) (hO : ∀ a, IsBinaryObservable (O a)) :
   102	    (fourierNaimarkData O hO).source = (fourierSquareMeasurement O hO).toSubmeasurement :=
   103	  Classical.choose_spec (oneMeasNaimark (fourierSquareMeasurement O hO).toSubmeasurement)
   104	
   105	/-- Formalization-only auxiliary lemma for the rounding below: distinct
   106	projectors of a one-measurement Naimark dilation are orthogonal, since they are
   107	projectors summing to at most the identity. -/
   108	private theorem liftedEffect_mul_liftedEffect_of_ne {α d : Type*}
   109	    [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α] [Fintype d] [DecidableEq d]
   110	    (data : OneMeasNaimarkData α d) {a b : Option α} (hab : a ≠ b) :
   111	    data.liftedEffect a * data.liftedEffect b = 0 :=
   112	  data.toProjSubMeasOption.outcome_orthogonal a b hab
   113	
   114	/-- Formalization-only auxiliary lemma for the compression identities below:
   115	the expectation-preservation identity of a one-measurement Naimark dilation,
   116	written with plain traces.  For every operator `X` on the original space,
   117	`Tr((X ⊗ |⊥⟩⟨⊥|) P̂_a) = Tr(X M_a)`. -/
   118	private theorem trace_kronecker_auxProjector_mul_liftedEffect {α d : Type*}
   119	    [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α] [Fintype d] [DecidableEq d]
   120	    (data : OneMeasNaimarkData α d) (X : Op d) (a : α) :
   121	    Matrix.trace (Matrix.kronecker X (naimarkAuxProjector α) * data.liftedEffect (some a)) =
   122	      Matrix.trace (X * data.source.effect a) := by
   123	  have h := data.expectation_preservation X a
   124	  simp only [normalizedTrace, oneMeasLiftedDensity, smul_mul_assoc, Matrix.trace_smul,
   125	    smul_eq_mul, Fintype.card_prod, Nat.cast_mul] at h
   126	  rcases isEmpty_or_nonempty d with hd | hd
   127	  · simp [Matrix.trace]
   128	  · have hd0 : (Fintype.card d : ℂ) ≠ 0 := Nat.cast_ne_zero.mpr Fintype.card_ne_zero
   129	    have hα : (Fintype.card (Option α) : ℂ) ≠ 0 := Nat.cast_ne_zero.mpr Fintype.card_ne_zero
   130	    rw [mul_comm (Fintype.card d : ℂ), mul_div_mul_left _ _ hα, div_left_inj' hd0] at h
   131	    exact h.symm
   132	
   133	/-! ## Folding the residual outcome into the zero Fourier outcome -/
   134	
   135	/-- The rounded Fourier projective measurement `{C^u}` on `ι × Option (F_2^t)`,
   136	obtained from the Naimark dilation of the Fourier-square POVM by folding the
   137	residual outcome `none` into the zero Fourier outcome.  For `u ≠ 0` the
   138	projector is the dilated projector of the outcome `u`; for `u = 0` it is the
   139	complement of the sum of the dilated projectors of the nonzero outcomes, so
   140	that the family resolves the identity on the enlarged space.  This is the
   141	projective measurement `{C^u}` of `references/nv-paper/fullpaper.tex:1099-1100`. -/
   142	def roundedFourierPVM {t : ℕ} {ι : Type} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
   143	    (O : (Fin t → ZMod 2) → Op ι) (hO : ∀ a, IsBinaryObservable (O a))
   144	    (u : Fin t → ZMod 2) : Op (ι × Option (Fin t → ZMod 2)) :=
   145	  if u = 0 then
   146	    1 - ∑ v ∈ Finset.univ.erase 0, (fourierNaimarkData O hO).liftedEffect (some v)
   147	  else (fourierNaimarkData O hO).liftedEffect (some u)
   148	
   149	/-- Formalization-only auxiliary lemma for `roundedFourierPVM`: the sum of the
   150	dilated projectors of the nonzero Fourier outcomes absorbs each of them on the
   151	left. -/
   152	private theorem sum_erase_mul_liftedEffect {t : ℕ} {ι : Type} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
   153	    (O : (Fin t → ZMod 2) → Op ι) (hO : ∀ a, IsBinaryObservable (O a))
   154	    {v : Fin t → ZMod 2} (hv : v ≠ 0) :
   155	    (∑ w ∈ Finset.univ.erase 0, (fourierNaimarkData O hO).liftedEffect (some w)) *
   156	        (fourierNaimarkData O hO).liftedEffect (some v) =
   157	      (fourierNaimarkData O hO).liftedEffect (some v) := by
   158	  rw [Finset.sum_mul, Finset.sum_eq_single v]
   159	  · exact ((fourierNaimarkData O hO).lifted_isProj (some v)).isIdempotentElem.eq
   160	  · intro w _ hwv
   161	    exact liftedEffect_mul_liftedEffect_of_ne _ (fun h => hwv (Option.some_inj.mp h))
   162	  · intro hv'
   163	    exact absurd (Finset.mem_erase.mpr ⟨hv, Finset.mem_univ v⟩) hv'
   164	
   165	/-- Formalization-only auxiliary lemma for `roundedFourierPVM`: the sum of the
   166	dilated projectors of the nonzero Fourier outcomes is a projector, its summands
   167	being mutually orthogonal projectors. -/
   168	private theorem isProj_sum_erase {t : ℕ} {ι : Type} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
   169	    (O : (Fin t → ZMod 2) → Op ι) (hO : ∀ a, IsBinaryObservable (O a)) :
   170	    IsProj (∑ w ∈ Finset.univ.erase 0, (fourierNaimarkData O hO).liftedEffect (some w)) := by
   171	  refine { isIdempotentElem := ?_, isSelfAdjoint := ?_ }
   172	  · unfold IsIdempotentElem
   173	    rw [Finset.mul_sum]
   174	    refine Finset.sum_congr rfl ?_
   175	    intro w hw
   176	    exact sum_erase_mul_liftedEffect O hO (Finset.ne_of_mem_erase hw)
   177	  · rw [isSelfAdjoint_iff, star_sum]
   178	    refine Finset.sum_congr rfl ?_
   179	    intro w _
   180	    exact ((fourierNaimarkData O hO).lifted_isProj (some w)).isSelfAdjoint.star_eq
   181	
   182	/-- Formalization-only auxiliary lemma for `roundedFourierPVM`: the sum of the
   183	dilated projectors of the nonzero Fourier outcomes absorbs each of them on the
   184	right, by taking adjoints in the left absorption. -/
   185	private theorem liftedEffect_mul_sum_erase {t : ℕ} {ι : Type} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
   186	    (O : (Fin t → ZMod 2) → Op ι) (hO : ∀ a, IsBinaryObservable (O a))
   187	    {v : Fin t → ZMod 2} (hv : v ≠ 0) :
   188	    (fourierNaimarkData O hO).liftedEffect (some v) *
   189	        (∑ w ∈ Finset.univ.erase 0, (fourierNaimarkData O hO).liftedEffect (some w)) =
   190	      (fourierNaimarkData O hO).liftedEffect (some v) := by
   191	  have h := congrArg Matrix.conjTranspose (sum_erase_mul_liftedEffect O hO hv)
   192	  rwa [Matrix.conjTranspose_mul, (isProj_sum_erase O hO).isSelfAdjoint.isHermitian.eq,
   193	    ((fourierNaimarkData O hO).lifted_isProj (some v)).isSelfAdjoint.isHermitian.eq] at h
   194	
   195	/-- Every rounded Fourier projector is an orthogonal projection. -/
   196	theorem roundedFourierPVM_isProj {t : ℕ} {ι : Type} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
   197	    (O : (Fin t → ZMod 2) → Op ι) (hO : ∀ a, IsBinaryObservable (O a))
   198	    (u : Fin t → ZMod 2) :
   199	    IsProj (roundedFourierPVM O hO u) := by
   200	  unfold roundedFourierPVM
   201	  by_cases hu : u = 0
   202	  · rw [if_pos hu]
   203	    exact (isProj_sum_erase O hO).one_sub
   204	  · rw [if_neg hu]
   205	    exact (fourierNaimarkData O hO).lifted_isProj (some u)
   206	
   207	/-- The rounded Fourier projectors resolve the identity on the enlarged space. -/
   208	theorem roundedFourierPVM_sum_eq_one {t : ℕ} {ι : Type} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
   209	    (O : (Fin t → ZMod 2) → Op ι) (hO : ∀ a, IsBinaryObservable (O a)) :
   210	    ∑ u : Fin t → ZMod 2, roundedFourierPVM O hO u = 1 := by
   211	  rw [← Finset.add_sum_erase Finset.univ _ (Finset.mem_univ (0 : Fin t → ZMod 2))]
   212	  have hrest : ∑ u ∈ Finset.univ.erase 0, roundedFourierPVM O hO u =
   213	      ∑ u ∈ Finset.univ.erase 0, (fourierNaimarkData O hO).liftedEffect (some u) := by
   214	    refine Finset.sum_congr rfl ?_
   215	    intro u hu
   216	    unfold roundedFourierPVM
   217	    rw [if_neg (Finset.ne_of_mem_erase hu)]
   218	  rw [hrest]
   219	  unfold roundedFourierPVM
   220	  rw [if_pos rfl, sub_add_cancel]
   221	
   222	/-- Distinct rounded Fourier projectors are orthogonal.  This is the
   223	orthogonality of the projectors `C^u` invoked at
   224	`references/nv-paper/fullpaper.tex:1103-1104`. -/
   225	theorem roundedFourierPVM_mul_eq_zero_of_ne {t : ℕ} {ι : Type} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
   226	    (O : (Fin t → ZMod 2) → Op ι) (hO : ∀ a, IsBinaryObservable (O a))
   227	    {u v : Fin t → ZMod 2} (huv : u ≠ v) :
   228	    roundedFourierPVM O hO u * roundedFourierPVM O hO v = 0 := by
   229	  unfold roundedFourierPVM
   230	  by_cases hu : u = 0 <;> by_cases hv : v = 0
   231	  · exact absurd (hu.trans hv.symm) huv
   232	  · rw [if_pos hu, if_neg hv, Matrix.sub_mul, Matrix.one_mul,
   233	      sum_erase_mul_liftedEffect O hO hv, sub_self]
   234	  · rw [if_neg hu, if_pos hv, Matrix.mul_sub, Matrix.mul_one,
   235	      liftedEffect_mul_sum_erase O hO hu, sub_self]
   236	  · rw [if_neg hu, if_neg hv]
   237	    exact liftedEffect_mul_liftedEffect_of_ne _ (fun h => huv (Option.some_inj.mp h))
   238	
   239	/-- The compression identity of the rounded Fourier projective measurement: for
   240	every operator `X` on the original space,
   241	`Tr((X ⊗ |anc⟩⟨anc|) C^u) = Tr(X B^u)`, where `B^u = (hat O^u)^2` is the
   242	Fourier-square effect.  For a nonzero outcome this is the expectation
   243	preservation of the one-measurement Naimark dilation; for the zero outcome it
   244	follows from the resolution of the identity by the `B^u`.  This is the sense in
   245	which `{C^u}` simulates `{B^u}` at `references/nv-paper/fullpaper.tex:1099-1100`. -/
   246	theorem trace_heteroKron_mul_roundedFourierPVM {t : ℕ} {ι : Type} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
   247	    (O : (Fin t → ZMod 2) → Op ι) (hO : ∀ a, IsBinaryObservable (O a))
   248	    (X : Op ι) (u : Fin t → ZMod 2) :
   249	    Matrix.trace (heteroKron X (ancProj (naimarkAncilla t)) * roundedFourierPVM O hO u) =
   250	      Matrix.trace (X * (operatorFourier O u * operatorFourier O u)) := by
   251	  have hP : ∀ v : Fin t → ZMod 2,
   252	      Matrix.trace (heteroKron X (ancProj (naimarkAncilla t)) *
   253	          (fourierNaimarkData O hO).liftedEffect (some v)) =
   254	        Matrix.trace (X * (operatorFourier O v * operatorFourier O v)) := by
   255	    intro v
   256	    rw [ancProj_naimarkAncilla]
   257	    unfold heteroKron
   258	    rw [trace_kronecker_auxProjector_mul_liftedEffect, fourierNaimarkData_source]
   259	    rfl
   260	  unfold roundedFourierPVM
   261	  by_cases hu : u = 0
   262	  · rw [if_pos hu]
   263	    subst hu
   264	    have hone :
   265	        Matrix.trace (heteroKron X (ancProj (naimarkAncilla t)) * 1) = Matrix.trace (X * 1) := by
   266	      rw [Matrix.mul_one, Matrix.mul_one, ancProj_naimarkAncilla]
   267	      unfold heteroKron naimarkAuxProjector
   268	      simpa using Matrix.trace_kronecker X
   269	        (Matrix.single (none : Option (Fin t → ZMod 2)) none (1 : ℂ))
   270	    have hB : X * (operatorFourier O 0 * operatorFourier O 0) =
   271	        X * 1 - ∑ v ∈ Finset.univ.erase 0, X * (operatorFourier O v * operatorFourier O v) := by
   272	      rw [← Finset.mul_sum, ← Matrix.mul_sub]
   273	      congr 1
   274	      rw [eq_sub_iff_add_eq]
   275	      exact (Finset.add_sum_erase Finset.univ
   276	        (fun v => operatorFourier O v * operatorFourier O v) (Finset.mem_univ 0)).trans
   277	        (sum_operatorFourier_sq_eq_one O hO)
   278	    rw [hB, Matrix.mul_sub, Finset.mul_sum, Matrix.trace_sub, Matrix.trace_sub,
   279	      Matrix.trace_sum, Matrix.trace_sum, hone]
   280	    congr 1
   281	    exact Finset.sum_congr rfl (fun v _ => hP v)
   282	  · rw [if_neg hu]
   283	    exact hP u
   284	
   285	/-! ## The rounded observables -/
   286	
   287	/-- The rounded observables `L^a = ∑_u (-1)^{u·a} C^u`, the signed sums of the
   288	rounded Fourier projectors.  These are the observables `𝒜(a)` introduced at
   289	`references/nv-paper/fullpaper.tex:1100-1102`; the character `(-1)^{u·a}` is
   290	`booleanCharacter u a`. -/
   291	def roundedObservable {t : ℕ} {ι : Type} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
   292	    (O : (Fin t → ZMod 2) → Op ι) (hO : ∀ a, IsBinaryObservable (O a))
   293	    (a : Fin t → ZMod 2) : Op (ι × Option (Fin t → ZMod 2)) :=
   294	  ∑ u : Fin t → ZMod 2, booleanCharacter u a • roundedFourierPVM O hO u
   295	
   296	/-- The exact linearity `L^a L^b = L^{a+b}` of the rounded observables, for
   297	every pair of Boolean-group elements.  Expanding the product, the orthogonality
   298	and idempotence of the projectors `C^u` leave only the diagonal terms, and the
   299	characters multiply.  This is the deduction at
   300	`references/nv-paper/fullpaper.tex:1103-1104`. -/
   301	theorem roundedObservable_mul {t : ℕ} {ι : Type} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
   302	    (O : (Fin t → ZMod 2) → Op ι) (hO : ∀ a, IsBinaryObservable (O a))
   303	    (a b : Fin t → ZMod 2) :
   304	    roundedObservable O hO a * roundedObservable O hO b = roundedObservable O hO (a + b) := by
   305	  unfold roundedObservable
   306	  rw [Finset.sum_mul]
   307	  refine Finset.sum_congr rfl ?_
   308	  intro u _
   309	  rw [Finset.mul_sum, Finset.sum_eq_single u]
   310	  · rw [smul_mul_assoc, mul_smul_comm, smul_smul,
   311	      (roundedFourierPVM_isProj O hO u).isIdempotentElem.eq, ← booleanCharacter_add_right]
   312	  · intro v _ hvu
   313	    rw [smul_mul_assoc, mul_smul_comm, roundedFourierPVM_mul_eq_zero_of_ne O hO hvu.symm,
   314	      smul_zero, smul_zero]
   315	  · intro hu
   316	    exact absurd (Finset.mem_univ u) hu
   317	
   318	/-- The rounded observable at the zero group element is the identity. -/
   319	theorem roundedObservable_zero {t : ℕ} {ι : Type} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
   320	    (O : (Fin t → ZMod 2) → Op ι) (hO : ∀ a, IsBinaryObservable (O a)) :
   321	    roundedObservable O hO 0 = 1 := by
   322	  simp [roundedObservable, roundedFourierPVM_sum_eq_one]
   323	
   324	/-- The rounded observables are Hermitian: the characters are real and the
   325	rounded Fourier projectors are self-adjoint. -/
   326	theorem roundedObservable_isHermitian {t : ℕ} {ι : Type} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
   327	    (O : (Fin t → ZMod 2) → Op ι) (hO : ∀ a, IsBinaryObservable (O a))
   328	    (a : Fin t → ZMod 2) :
   329	    (roundedObservable O hO a).IsHermitian := by
   330	  rw [Matrix.IsHermitian, roundedObservable, Matrix.conjTranspose_sum]
   331	  refine Finset.sum_congr rfl ?_
   332	  intro u _
   333	  rw [Matrix.conjTranspose_smul, star_booleanCharacter,
   334	    (roundedFourierPVM_isProj O hO u).isSelfAdjoint.isHermitian.eq]
   335	
   336	/-- Every rounded observable is a binary observable: it is Hermitian, and its
   337	square is `L^{a+a} = L^0 = 1` by exact linearity. -/
   338	theorem roundedObservable_isBinaryObservable {t : ℕ} {ι : Type} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
   339	    (O : (Fin t → ZMod 2) → Op ι) (hO : ∀ a, IsBinaryObservable (O a))
   340	    (a : Fin t → ZMod 2) :
   341	    IsBinaryObservable (roundedObservable O hO a) := by
   342	  refine ⟨roundedObservable_isHermitian O hO a, ?_⟩
   343	  have haa : a + a = 0 := by
   344	    ext i
   345	    exact CharTwo.add_self_eq_zero (a i)
   346	  rw [roundedObservable_mul, haa, roundedObservable_zero]
   347	
   348	/-- The compression identity of the rounded observables: for every operator `X`
   349	on the original space,
   350	`Tr((X ⊗ |anc⟩⟨anc|) L^a) = Tr(X ∑_u (-1)^{u·a} B^u)`.  The right-hand side
   351	is the character sum of the Fourier-square POVM whose overlap with `O^a` is
   352	certified by `one_sub_error_le_avg_overlap_fourierSquare`; this is the passage
   353	from `Tr_{ρ'}(A(a) 𝒜(a))` to `Tr_ρ(A(a) ∑_u (-1)^{u·a} (hat A^u)^2)` at
   354	`references/nv-paper/fullpaper.tex:1105-1110`. -/
   355	theorem trace_heteroKron_mul_roundedObservable {t : ℕ} {ι : Type} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
   356	    (O : (Fin t → ZMod 2) → Op ι) (hO : ∀ a, IsBinaryObservable (O a))
   357	    (X : Op ι) (a : Fin t → ZMod 2) :
   358	    Matrix.trace (heteroKron X (ancProj (naimarkAncilla t)) * roundedObservable O hO a) =
   359	      Matrix.trace (X * ∑ u : Fin t → ZMod 2, booleanCharacter u a •
   360	        (operatorFourier O u * operatorFourier O u)) := by
   361	  simp only [roundedObservable, Finset.mul_sum, Matrix.trace_sum, mul_smul_comm,
   362	    Matrix.trace_smul, trace_heteroKron_mul_roundedFourierPVM]
   363	
   364	end

1	import MIPStarRE.Quantum.FiniteMatrix.NormalizedTrace
     2	
     3	/-!
     4	# Matrix-valued measurements for the MIP*=RE project
     5	
     6	This file provides the matrix-valued measurement layer used by the LDT formalization.
     7	
     8	## Main definitions
     9	
    10	* `Submeasurement` — a family of PSD matrices summing to at most the identity.
    11	* `Measurement` — a family of PSD matrices summing to exactly the identity.
    12	* `Submeasurement.postprocess` — data-processed submeasurements via answer relabeling.
    13	* `Measurement.postprocess` — the paper's postprocessing proposition for complete POVMs.
    14	* `inconsistency` — the off-diagonal mass `∑_{a ≠ b} τ(M_a N_b)`.
    15	* `diagOverlap` — the diagonal mass `∑_a τ(M_a N_a)`.
    16	
    17	## References
    18	
    19	This file builds the project's finite-dimensional measurement layer on top of
    20	the normalized-trace and positive-operator facts in `MIPStarRE.Quantum.FiniteMatrix`
    21	for the quantum formalization in `references/ldt-paper/`.
    22	-/
    23	
    24	open scoped BigOperators MatrixOrder Matrix ComplexOrder
    25	
    26	namespace MIPStarRE.Quantum
    27	
    28	/-! ## Submeasurements and measurements -/
    29	
    30	/--
    31	A submeasurement on a finite answer type `α` is a family of PSD matrices
    32	`M : α → Op d` with `∑ a, M a ≤ 1`.
    33	-/
    34	structure Submeasurement (α : Type*) [Fintype α] (d : Type*) [Fintype d] [DecidableEq d] where
    35	  /-- The effect operators. -/
    36	  effect : α → Op d
    37	  /-- Each effect is positive semidefinite. -/
    38	  pos : ∀ a, 0 ≤ effect a
    39	  /-- The effects sum to at most the identity. -/
    40	  sum_le_one : ∑ a, effect a ≤ 1
    41	
    42	/--
    43	A measurement is a submeasurement whose effects sum exactly to the identity.
    44	-/
    45	structure Measurement (α : Type*) [Fintype α] (d : Type*) [Fintype d] [DecidableEq d]
    46	    extends Submeasurement α d where
    47	  /-- The effects sum to the identity. -/
    48	  sum_eq_one : ∑ a, effect a = 1
    49	
    50	/-! ## Totals and postprocessing -/
    51	
    52	namespace Submeasurement
    53	
    54	variable {d : Type*} [Fintype d] [DecidableEq d]
    55	variable {α β : Type*} [Fintype α] [Fintype β]
    56	
    57	/-! ### Totals and postprocessing -/
    58	
    59	/-- The total operator `∑ a, M_a`. -/
    60	noncomputable def total (M : Submeasurement α d) : Op d :=
    61	  ∑ a, M.effect a
    62	
    63	/--
    64	Data processing: relabel the answer set by `f : α → β`, summing the effects over
    65	fibers.
    66	-/
    67	noncomputable def postprocess [DecidableEq α] [DecidableEq β]
    68	    (M : Submeasurement α d) (f : α → β) : Submeasurement β d where
    69	  effect b := ∑ a ∈ Finset.univ.filter (fun a => f a = b), M.effect a
    70	  pos b := Finset.sum_nonneg fun a _ => M.pos a
    71	  sum_le_one := by
    72	    calc
    73	      ∑ b, ∑ a ∈ Finset.univ.filter (fun a => f a = b), M.effect a
    74	          = ∑ a, M.effect a := Finset.sum_fiberwise Finset.univ f M.effect
    75	      _ ≤ 1 := M.sum_le_one
    76	
    77	/-- Restatement of `sum_le_one` in terms of the named total operator. -/

   101	/--

   104	This constructor keeps the equality proof as the primary hypothesis and derives
   105	the inherited submeasurement inequality automatically.  It is useful at paper

   108	def ofSumEqOne (effect : α → Op d) (pos : ∀ a, 0 ≤ effect a)

   111	  pos := pos

   113	  sum_eq_one := sum_eq_one

   116	theorem total_eq_one (M : Measurement α d) :
   117	    M.total = 1 :=

   120	/--
   121	Postprocess a complete measurement by relabeling outcomes.
   122	
   123	This formalizes `references/ldt-paper/preliminaries.tex:169--180`: regrouping
   124	the effects along the fibers of `f` preserves the total operator, so a POVM
   125	remains a POVM after postprocessing.

   127	noncomputable def postprocess [DecidableEq α] [DecidableEq β]
   128	    (M : Measurement α d) (f : α → β) : Measurement β d where
   129	  toSubmeasurement := M.toSubmeasurement.postprocess f
   130	  sum_eq_one := by
   131	    calc
   132	      ∑ b, ∑ a ∈ Finset.univ.filter (fun a => f a = b), M.effect a
   133	          = ∑ a, M.effect a := Finset.sum_fiberwise Finset.univ f M.effect

   143	    (M : Measurement α d) (f : α → β) :
   144	    (M.postprocess f).toSubmeasurement = M.toSubmeasurement.postprocess f :=
   145	  rfl

   104	\begin{theorem}[Quantum linearity test~\cite{Natarajan2017Linearity}]
   105		\label{thm:linearity}
   106		\lean{MIPStarRE.QPBT.IsBinaryObservable, MIPStarRE.QPBT.stateDepDistSq}
   107		\lean{MIPStarRE.QPBT.exists_exactly_linear_observables}
   108		\lean{MIPStarRE.QPBT.exists_exactly_linear_observables_binaryObservableDistSq}
   109		\leanok
   110		\uses{def:povm-conventions, lem:binary-measurement-distance}
   111		Let $t$ be a positive integer and $\delta \ge 0$. Let $\rho$ be a
   112		density operator on a Hilbert space $\hilb$ and let
   113		$\{\mathcal{O}^u\}$ be a set of binary observables indexed by
   114		$u \in \F_2^t$ acting on $\hilb$, such that on average over $u, u'$
   115		chosen uniformly at random from $\F_2^t$,
   116		\[
   117			\E_{u,u'} \Tr\big(\mathcal{O}^u \, \mathcal{O}^{u'} \,
   118			\mathcal{O}^{u+u'} \, \rho\big) \ge 1 - \delta\,.
   119		\]
   120		Then there exist a Hilbert space $\hilb'$, a pure state
   121		$\ket{\mathrm{anc}} \in \hilb'$, and binary observables
   122		$\{\mathcal{L}^u\}$ indexed by $u \in \F_2^t$ acting on
   123		$\hilb \ot \hilb'$ such that, writing
   124		$\rho' = \rho \ot \ket{\mathrm{anc}}\bra{\mathrm{anc}}$, the exact
   125		linearity
   126		\[
   127			\mathcal{L}^u \, \mathcal{L}^{u'} = \mathcal{L}^{u+u'}
   128		\]
   129		holds for all $u, u' \in \F_2^t$, and
   130		\[
   131			\E_{u} \, d_{\rho'}\big(\mathcal{L}^u,\ \mathcal{O}^u \ot
   132			\Id_{\hilb'}\big)^2 \le 2\delta\,,
   133		\]
   134		where the expectation is over $u$ chosen uniformly at random from
   135		$\F_2^t$ and
   136		$d_{\sigma}(S,T)
   137		= \big(\Tr\big((S-T)^\dagger (S-T)\, \sigma\big)\big)^{1/2}$
   138		denotes the state-dependent distance with respect to a density
   139		operator $\sigma$. Equivalently, in the distance $d^{\mathrm{bin}}_\sigma$
   140		between the binary projective measurements associated with the
   141		observables (Lemma~\ref{lem:binary-measurement-distance}),
   142		\[
   143			\E_{u} \, d^{\mathrm{bin}}_{\rho'}\big(\mathcal{L}^u,\
   144			\mathcal{O}^u \ot \Id_{\hilb'}\big)^2 \le \delta\,.
   145		\]
   146		The cited source prints the first bound with $\delta$ in place of
   147		$2\delta$; that normalization is false, and the bounds stated here are
   148		the ones its argument establishes
   149		(Remark~\ref{rem:linearity-distance-normalization}).
   150	\end{theorem}

   153		\uses{lem:binary-measurement-distance, lem:boolean-fourier-transform,
   154			lem:naimark-helper}

   156		whose Fourier--Naimark argument is followed; \cite{Ji2020MIPStar} invokes
   157		the result without proof. Write $\chi_v(u) = (-1)^{v \cdot u}$ and
   158		$\widehat{\mathcal{O}}^v = \E_u \, \chi_v(u) \, \mathcal{O}^u$ as in
   159		Lemma~\ref{lem:boolean-fourier-transform}.
   160	
   161		\emph{From the correlation to the multiplicative defect.} For
   162		$u, u' \in \F_2^t$, expanding
   163		$(\mathcal{O}^u \mathcal{O}^{u'} - \mathcal{O}^{u+u'})^\dagger
   164		(\mathcal{O}^u \mathcal{O}^{u'} - \mathcal{O}^{u+u'})$ with
   165		$(\mathcal{O}^w)^2 = \Id$ and $\Tr \rho = 1$, as in the proof of
   166		Lemma~\ref{lem:binary-measurement-distance}, gives

   169			= 2 - 2 \Re \Tr\big(\mathcal{O}^{u'} \mathcal{O}^u
   170			\mathcal{O}^{u'+u} \rho\big)\,,
   171		\]

   173		coordinates of the uniform pair $(u,u')$, the hypothesis yields
   174		$\E_{u,u'} d_\rho(\mathcal{O}^u \mathcal{O}^{u'},
   175		\mathcal{O}^{u+u'})^2 \le 2\delta$. No commutation among the
   176		observables is used.
   177	
   178		\emph{The Fourier-square measurement and its Naimark rounding.} By
   179		Lemma~\ref{lem:boolean-fourier-transform} the operators
   180		$B^v = (\widehat{\mathcal{O}}^v)^2$ are positive semidefinite and sum to
   181		$\Id$, so they form a POVM indexed by $\F_2^t$.

   189		$B^v$ themselves sum to $\Id$. Set

   191		Hermitian, and the orthogonality of the $C^v$ together with
   192		$\chi_v(u) \chi_v(u') = \chi_v(u+u')$ gives
   193		$\mathcal{L}^u \mathcal{L}^{u'} = \mathcal{L}^{u+u'}$ for all $u, u'$;
   194		in particular $(\mathcal{L}^u)^2 = \mathcal{L}^0 = \sum_v C^v = \Id$,
   195		so the $\mathcal{L}^u$ are binary observables.
   196	
   197		\emph{The distance/defect identity.} Since $\mathcal{L}^u$ and
   198		$\mathcal{O}^u \ot \Id$ are binary observables and $\rho'$ is a density
   199		operator, Lemma~\ref{lem:binary-measurement-distance} gives
   200		$d_{\rho'}(\mathcal{L}^u, \mathcal{O}^u \ot \Id)^2
   201		= 2 - 2 \Re \Tr(\mathcal{L}^u (\mathcal{O}^u \ot \Id) \rho')$.
   202		Compressing along $\ket{\mathrm{anc}}$,
   203		$\Re \Tr(\mathcal{L}^u (\mathcal{O}^u \ot \Id) \rho')
   204		= \Re \Tr(\mathcal{O}^u \sum_v \chi_v(u) B^v \rho)$; averaging over $u$
   205		turns $\E_u \chi_v(u) \mathcal{O}^u$ into $\widehat{\mathcal{O}}^v$, and
   206		expanding the three Fourier coefficients and summing the characters
   207		(Lemma~\ref{lem:boolean-fourier-transform}) gives
   208		\[
   209			\E_u \Re \Tr\big(\mathcal{L}^u (\mathcal{O}^u \ot \Id) \rho'\big)
   210			= \sum_v \Re \Tr\big((\widehat{\mathcal{O}}^v)^3 \rho\big)
   211			= \E_{u,u'} \Re \Tr\big(\mathcal{O}^u \mathcal{O}^{u'}
   212			\mathcal{O}^{u+u'} \rho\big)\,.
   213		\]
   214		Hence
   215		$\E_u d_{\rho'}(\mathcal{L}^u, \mathcal{O}^u \ot \Id)^2
   216		= 2 - 2 \E_{u,u'} \Re \Tr(\mathcal{O}^u \mathcal{O}^{u'}
   217		\mathcal{O}^{u+u'} \rho)
   218		= \E_{u,u'} d_\rho(\mathcal{O}^u \mathcal{O}^{u'},
   219		\mathcal{O}^{u+u'})^2 \le 2\delta$ by the first step. The measurement
   220		form follows by halving, through the normalization identity of
   221		Lemma~\ref{lem:binary-measurement-distance}.
   222

   229		Remark~\ref{rem:linearity-import} and addressed in the proof of
   230		Lemma~\ref{lem:qld-4-10}.
   231	\end{proof}

520		This is not a named statement of \cite{Natarajan2017Linearity}; it isolates
   521		the measurement to which Naimark's theorem is applied in the proof given
   522		there for Theorem~\ref{thm:linearity}
   523		(\texttt{references/nv-paper/fullpaper.tex:1096--1112}). Let
   524		$\{O(a)\}_{a \in \F_2^t}$ be a family of operators on $\hilb$, with Fourier
   525		coefficients $\widehat{O}^u$ and characters $\chi_u$ as in
   526		Lemma~\ref{lem:boolean-fourier-transform}, let $\rho$ be an operator on
   527		$\hilb$, and write $B^u = (\widehat{O}^u)^2$. With no hypothesis on the
   528		family or on $\rho$,
   529		\[
   530			\sum_u (\widehat{O}^u)^3 = \E_{a,b} \, O(a) \, O(b) \, O(a+b) ,
   531			\qquad
   532			\sum_u \Re \Tr\big((\widehat{O}^u)^3 \, \rho\big) = C_\rho(O) ,
   533		\]
   534		where $C_\rho(O)$ is the two-query correlation of
   535		Lemma~\ref{lem:blr-defect-identity}, and
   536		\[
   537			\E_a \, \Re \Tr\Big(O(a) \,
   538			\Big(\sum_u \chi_u(a) \, B^u\Big) \, \rho\Big)
   539			= \sum_u \Re \Tr\big((\widehat{O}^u)^3 \, \rho\big) .
   540		\]
   541		If every $O(a)$ is Hermitian, then every $B^u$ is positive semidefinite;
   542		if every $O(a)$ is a binary observable, then the $B^u$ are the effects of a
   543		POVM with outcomes in $\F_2^t$, the Fourier-square measurement. Finally,
   544		if $C_\rho(O) \ge 1 - \delta$, then
   545		\[
   546			1 - \delta \le \E_a \, \Re \Tr\Big(O(a) \,
   547			\Big(\sum_u \chi_u(a) \, B^u\Big) \, \rho\Big) .
   548		\]
   549	\end{lemma}
   550	\begin{proof}
   551		\leanok
   552		\uses{lem:boolean-characters, lem:boolean-fourier-transform}
   553		Expanding one Fourier coefficient at a time through the inversion formula
   554		of Lemma~\ref{lem:boolean-fourier-transform} and collapsing the inner
   555		character sum with Lemma~\ref{lem:boolean-characters} gives the cubic
   556		identity; multiplying it by $\rho$, taking the trace and passing to real
   557		parts gives the correlation identity, and the same expansion applied to
   558		$\sum_u \widehat{O}^u \, B^u$ gives the overlap identity. Positivity of
   559		$B^u$ holds because $\widehat{O}^u$ is Hermitian, so that
   560		$B^u = (\widehat{O}^u)^\dagger \widehat{O}^u$, and completeness is the
   561		identity $\sum_u (\widehat{O}^u)^2 = \Id$ of
   562		Lemma~\ref{lem:boolean-fourier-transform}. The final inequality
   563		substitutes the correlation hypothesis into the overlap identity.
   564	\end{proof}

   583		(\texttt{references/nv-paper/fullpaper.tex:1096--1112}) establishes, with
   584		the correlation hypothesis replaced by the mean multiplicative defect of
   585		Lemma~\ref{lem:blr-defect-identity}. Let $t$ be a positive integer, let
   586		$\eta \ge 0$, let $\rho$ be a density operator on $\hilb$, and let
   587		$\{\mathcal{O}^u\}_{u \in \F_2^t}$ be binary observables on $\hilb$ with
   588		\[
   589			\E_{u,u'} \, d_\rho\big(\mathcal{O}^u \, \mathcal{O}^{u'},\
   590			\mathcal{O}^{u+u'}\big)^2 \le \eta .
   591		\]

   593		$\ket{\mathrm{anc}} \in \hilb'$ and binary observables
   594		$\{\mathcal{L}^u\}_{u \in \F_2^t}$ on $\hilb \ot \hilb'$ such that
   595		$\mathcal{L}^u \mathcal{L}^{u'} = \mathcal{L}^{u+u'}$ for all
   596		$u, u' \in \F_2^t$ and, writing
   597		$\rho' = \rho \ot \ket{\mathrm{anc}}\bra{\mathrm{anc}}$, which is again a
   598		density operator,
   599		\[
   600			\E_u \, d_{\rho'}\big(\mathcal{L}^u,\ \mathcal{O}^u \ot
   601			\Id_{\hilb'}\big)^2 \le \eta .
   602		\]
   603		The bound is the specialization of the identity
   604		\[
   605			\E_u \, d_{\rho'}\big(\mathcal{L}^u,\ \mathcal{O}^u \ot
   606			\Id_{\hilb'}\big)^2
   607			= \E_{u,u'} \, d_\rho\big(\mathcal{O}^u \, \mathcal{O}^{u'},\
   608			\mathcal{O}^{u+u'}\big)^2 ,
   609		\]

   611		equal $2 - 2 \, C_\rho(\mathcal{O})$ for the two-query correlation
   612		$C_\rho(\mathcal{O})$ of Lemma~\ref{lem:blr-defect-identity}.
   613	
   614		This is the mathematical content of Theorem~\ref{thm:linearity}: the
   615		ancillary space and state are produced explicitly, and by
   616		Lemma~\ref{lem:blr-defect-identity} a correlation hypothesis
   617		$C_\rho(\mathcal{O}) \ge 1 - \delta$ is exactly the hypothesis above with
   618		$\eta = 2\delta$. The conclusion obtained from such a hypothesis is
   619		therefore the bound $2\delta$, which is the bound displayed in
   620		Theorem~\ref{thm:linearity}; the constant $2$ separating it from the bound
   621		$\delta$ printed in the source is the normalization recorded in
   622		Remark~\ref{rem:linearity-distance-normalization}. The present statement is
   623		the defect-parameterized form of that theorem, and the substitution
   624		$\eta = 2\delta$ is the whole of the proof of
   625		Theorem~\ref{thm:linearity} from it.
   626	\end{lemma}

   633		extra element $\bot$, and take $\ket{\mathrm{anc}} = \ket{\bot}$, the
   634		initial state of the auxiliary register in the one-measurement Naimark
   635		construction of Lemma~\ref{lem:naimark-helper}. Apply that construction to
   636		the Fourier-square POVM $\{B^u\}$ of
   637		Lemma~\ref{lem:fourier-square-measurement}. It returns
   638		projectors indexed by $\F_2^t \cup \{\bot\}$; the residual projector at
   639		$\bot$ is folded into the outcome $u = 0$, so that the resulting family
   640		$\{C^u\}_{u \in \F_2^t}$ is still a family of orthogonal projectors summing
   641		to $\Id_{\hilb \ot \hilb'}$ and still compresses to $B^u$ along
   642		$\ket{\mathrm{anc}}$, the latter because $\sum_u B^u = \Id_\hilb$. Set
   643		$\mathcal{L}^a = \sum_u \chi_u(a) \, C^u$; orthogonality of the $C^u$ and

   645		$\mathcal{L}^a \mathcal{L}^b = \mathcal{L}^{a+b}$ and

   647		the characters are real. Since $\rho'$ is a density operator and both
   648		$\mathcal{L}^a$ and $\mathcal{O}^a \ot \Id_{\hilb'}$ are binary

   658		$\Re \Tr\big(\mathcal{O}^a \, (\sum_u \chi_u(a) B^u) \, \rho\big)$.

   662		Lemma~\ref{lem:blr-defect-identity}. No commutation among the
   663		$\mathcal{O}^u$ is used. The hypothesis then bounds the average by $\eta$.
   664	\end{proof}

     4	/-!
     5	# The quantum linearity theorem
     6	
     7	This file states the external quantum-linearity result used to combine the
     8	binary observables produced in the point analysis.  The statement uses a
     9	positive semidefinite trace-one operator, and its conclusion adjoins a finite ancillary
    10	space on which the exactly linear observables act.
    11	
    12	## References
    13	
    14	The declaration is `thm:linearity` in
    15	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:82-180`.  The quotation in the
    16	QPBT paper is at
    17	`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:713-725`; the
    18	provider is Theorem 10 of Natarajan--Vidick, arXiv:1610.03574.
    19	-/
    20	
    21	open scoped BigOperators Matrix MatrixOrder ComplexOrder
    22	
    23	namespace MIPStarRE.QPBT
    24	
    25	open MIPStarRE.LDT
    26	open MIPStarRE.Quantum
    27	
    28	noncomputable section
    29	
    30	/-- A binary observable is a Hermitian operator whose square is the identity.
    31	This is the finite-matrix realization of `Obs(H)` in `thm:linearity`, blueprint
    32	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:82-180`, quoted at paper
    33	`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:713-725`. -/
    34	def IsBinaryObservable {ι : Type} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    35	    (O : Op ι) : Prop :=
    36	  O.IsHermitian ∧ O * O = 1
    37	
    38	/-- The rank-one density operator associated with an ancillary vector. -/
    39	noncomputable def ancProj {ι : Type} [Fintype ι]
    40	    (v : EuclideanSpace ℂ ι) : Op ι :=
    41	  let w := (EuclideanSpace.equiv ι ℂ) v
    42	  Matrix.vecMulVec w (star w)
    43	
    44	/-- Squared state-dependent distance between two operators.  This is the
    45	quantity `d_rho(S,T)^2` in `thm:linearity`, blueprint
    46	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:82-180`. -/
    47	noncomputable def stateDepDistSq {ι : Type} [Fintype ι]
    48	    (S T ρ : Op ι) : ℝ :=
    49	  (Matrix.trace ((S - T)ᴴ * (S - T) * ρ)).re
    50	
    51	/-- The quantum linearity theorem imported from Natarajan--Vidick.
    52	
    53	The statement is `thm:linearity` in
    54	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:82-145`; the QPBT paper quotes
    55	it at
    56	`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:713-725`.
    57	
    58	As recorded in `rem:linearity-import` (blueprint lines 147--180), this
    59	provider-faithful form imposes no upper bound on `δ`, preserves the error,
    60	asserts exact linearity for every pair, and averages closeness only over `u`.
    61	The paper quotation instead adds `δ ≤ 1`, phrases closeness pointwise under a
    62	pair quantifier, and appends `L 0 = 1`; those three deviations are not
    63	reproduced.  The identity at zero follows later from exact linearity and the
    64	binary-observable condition. -/
    65	theorem exists_exactly_linear_observables {ι : Type}
    66	    [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    67	    (t : ℕ) (ht : 0 < t) (δ : ℝ) (hδ : 0 ≤ δ)
    68	    (ρ : Op ι) (hρ : ρ.PosSemidef) (htrace : ρ.trace = 1)
    69	    (O : (Fin t → ZMod 2) → Op ι)
    70	    (hO : ∀ u, IsBinaryObservable (O u))
    71	    (hcorrelation :
    72	      1 - δ ≤ avgOver
    73	        (uniformDistribution
    74	          ((Fin t → ZMod 2) × (Fin t → ZMod 2)))
    75	        (fun pair =>
    76	          (Matrix.trace
    77	            (O pair.1 * O pair.2 * O (pair.1 + pair.2) * ρ)).re)) :
    78	    ∃ (ι' : Type) (_ : Fintype ι') (_ : DecidableEq ι')
    79	        (anc : EuclideanSpace ℂ ι'),
    80	      ‖anc‖ = 1 ∧
    81	        ∃ L : (Fin t → ZMod 2) → Op (ι × ι'),
    82	          (∀ u, IsBinaryObservable (L u)) ∧
    83	          (∀ u u', L u * L u' = L (u + u')) ∧
    84	          avgOver (uniformDistribution (Fin t → ZMod 2))
    85	              (fun u => stateDepDistSq (L u)
    86	                (heteroKron (O u) (1 : Op ι'))
    87	                (heteroKron ρ (ancProj anc))) ≤ δ := by

blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:6:This chapter records the vocabulary in which the quantum Pauli basis test and its analysis are phrased: two-player one-round games and tensor product strategies, the consistency and state-dependent distance calculus for families of measurements, and conditionally linear functions and distributions, the class of question distributions used by the tests of Chapter~\ref{chap:qpbt-test}. The presentation follows \cite{Ji2020MIPStar}; the distance calculus is imported there from \cite{Natarajan2018NEEXP} and \cite{Ji2020LowIndividualDegree}.
blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:225:	and we write $M^x_a \approx_\delta N^x_a$ to denote this when the state $\ket{\psi}$ and the distribution $\mu$ are clear from context. This distance is referred to as the \emph{state-dependent} distance. The principal case is that in which $\{M^x_a\}$ and $\{N^x_a\}$ are POVMs on $\mathcal H$, and we then speak of the state-dependent distance between the POVMs; but the relation is used for arbitrary operator families --- for instance for products of measurement operators, or for commutators compared against the identically zero family, as in Lemma~\ref{lem:commutation-analysis} below.
blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:243:We record several useful facts about the consistency measure and the state-dependent distance. For the statements imported without proof, readers are referred to Sections~4.4 and~4.5 of \cite{Natarajan2018NEEXP}.
blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:378:	Stated in the source without proof; it is Proposition 4.29 of \cite{Ji2020LowIndividualDegree}. The two hypotheses involving $C$ convert, via Lemma~\ref{fact:agreement}, into state-dependent closeness of $C^x_a \ot \Id_B$ to both $\Id_A \ot B^x_a$ and $\Id_A \ot D^x_a$, hence of $\Id_A \ot B^x_a$ to $\Id_A \ot D^x_a$ at cost $O(\delta+\gamma)$. The first consistency then transfers from $B$ to $D$ by expanding the off-diagonal mass and applying the Cauchy--Schwarz inequality, which turns the squared-distance bound into the term $2\sqrt{\delta+\gamma}$.
blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:401:The state-dependent distance is the right tool for reasoning about the closeness of measurement operators in a strategy. The following lemma converts joint consistency with a single projective measurement into an approximate commutation relation.
blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:579:	Stated in the source without proof; it is Fact 4.32 of \cite{Natarajan2018NEEXP}. Write the value difference as an average over $(x,y) \sim \mu$ of sums of terms of the form $\bra{\psi} (A^x_a - (A')^x_a) \ot B^y_b \ket{\psi}$ and $\bra{\psi} (A')^x_a \ot (B^y_b - (B')^y_b) \ket{\psi}$, replacing one player's measurements at a time. The Cauchy--Schwarz inequality bounds each group by the square root of the corresponding averaged squared state-dependent distance, and projectivity of one of the two strategies keeps the accompanying operator sums bounded, giving the total bound $O(\delta^{1/2})$.

    81	
    82	/-- The canonical complex additive character `x ↦ ω^{tr[x]}` on `F`. -/
    83	noncomputable abbrev ffChar : AddChar F ℂ :=
    84	  (ZMod.stdAddChar (N := p)).compAddMonoidHom (Algebra.trace (ZMod p) F).toAddMonoidHom
    85	
    86	omit [Fintype F] [DecidableEq F] in
    87	@[simp] theorem ffChar_apply (x : F) :
    88	    ffChar (p := p) (F := F) x =
    89	      ZMod.stdAddChar (N := p) (ffTrace (p := p) (F := F) x) :=
    90	  rfl
    91	
    92	omit [Fintype F] [DecidableEq F] in
    93	private theorem ffTrace_nondegenerate [Finite F] (a : F) (ha : a ≠ 0) :
    94	    ∃ b : F, ffTrace (p := p) (F := F) (a * b) ≠ 0 := by
    95	  haveI : CharP F p := (Algebra.charP_iff (ZMod p) F p).mp (ZMod.charP p)
    96	  have hp : p = ringChar F := by
    97	    simpa using (ringChar.eq F p).symm
    98	  subst p
    99	  simpa [ffTrace] using (FiniteField.trace_to_zmod_nondegenerate F (a := a) ha)
   100	
   101	omit [Fintype F] [DecidableEq F] in
   102	private theorem ffChar_ne_zero [Finite F] : ffChar (p := p) (F := F) ≠ 0 := by
   103	  rw [AddChar.ne_zero_iff]
   104	  obtain ⟨a, ha0⟩ :=
   105	    ffTrace_nondegenerate (p := p) (F := F) (a := (1 : F)) one_ne_zero
   106	  have ha : ffTrace (p := p) (F := F) a ≠ 0 := by
   107	    simpa using ha0
   108	  refine ⟨a, ?_⟩
   109	  rw [ffChar_apply]
   110	  intro h
   111	  exact ha ((AddChar.IsPrimitive.zmod_char_eq_one_iff p (ZMod.isPrimitive_stdAddChar p) _).mp h)
   112	
   113	/-- Paper label `prop:fourier-fact-scalar`.
   114	
   115	The Fourier orthogonality relation for the finite field `F`: the expectation
   116	of the additive character `ω^{tr[x·a]}` over `x ∈ F` equals `1` when `a = 0`
   117	and `0` otherwise. -/
   118	theorem fourier_fact_scalar (a : F) :
   119	    𝔼 x : F, ffChar (p := p) (F := F) (x * a) =
   120	      if a = 0 then (1 : ℂ) else 0 := by
   121	  let ψ : AddChar F ℂ := (ffChar (p := p) (F := F)).mulShift a
   122	  calc
   123	    𝔼 x : F, ffChar (p := p) (F := F) (x * a) = 𝔼 x : F, ψ x := by
   124	      simp [ψ, AddChar.mulShift_apply, mul_comm]
   125	    _ = if ψ = 0 then (1 : ℂ) else 0 := AddChar.expect_eq_ite ψ
   126	    _ = if a = 0 then (1 : ℂ) else 0 := by
   127	      by_cases ha : a = 0
   128	      · have hψ : ψ = 0 := by
   129	          ext x
   130	          simp [ψ, ha]
   131	        simp [ha, hψ]
   132	      · have hψ : ψ ≠ 0 := by

   139	section Vector
   140	
   141	variable {m : ℕ}
   142	
   143	-- We define `ffDotProduct` directly rather than reusing `Matrix.dotProduct` to avoid
   144	-- pulling in the full `Mathlib.Data.Matrix.Basic` import. The definitions are identical.
   145	/-- The standard dot product on `F^m`. -/
   146	def ffDotProduct (u v : Fin m → F) : F :=
   147	  ∑ i, u i * v i
   148	
   149	/-- The additive character `u ↦ ω^{tr[⟨u, v⟩]}` on `F^m`. -/
   150	noncomputable def ffVecChar (v : Fin m → F) : AddChar (Fin m → F) ℂ :=
   151	  (ffChar (p := p) (F := F)).compAddMonoidHom
   152	    { toFun := fun u => ffDotProduct u v
   153	      map_zero' := by simp [ffDotProduct]
   154	      map_add' := by
   155	        intro u w
   156	        simp [ffDotProduct, add_mul, Finset.sum_add_distrib] }
   157	
   158	omit [Fintype F] [DecidableEq F] in
   159	@[simp] theorem ffVecChar_apply (u v : Fin m → F) :
   160	    ffVecChar (p := p) (F := F) v u =
   161	      ffChar (p := p) (F := F) (ffDotProduct u v) :=
   162	  rfl
   163	
   164	omit [Fintype F] [DecidableEq F] in

   166	    ffVecChar (p := p) (F := F) v ≠ 0 := by
   167	  rw [AddChar.ne_zero_iff]
   168	  obtain ⟨i, hi⟩ : ∃ i, v i ≠ 0 := by
   169	    simpa [funext_iff] using hv
   170	  obtain ⟨b, hb0⟩ :=
   171	    ffTrace_nondegenerate (p := p) (F := F) (a := v i) hi
   172	  have hb : ffTrace (p := p) (F := F) (b * v i) ≠ 0 := by
   173	    simpa [mul_comm] using hb0
   174	  refine ⟨Pi.single i b, ?_⟩

   176	    unfold ffDotProduct
   177	    rw [Finset.sum_eq_single i]

   180	      simp [hji]

   184	  intro h

   187	/-- Paper label `prop:fourier-fact-vector`.
   188	
   189	The vector version of Fourier orthogonality: the expectation of the additive
   190	character `ω^{tr[⟨u, v⟩]}` over `u ∈ F^m` equals `1` when `v = 0`
   191	and `0` otherwise. -/
   192	theorem fourier_fact_vector (v : Fin m → F) :
   193	    𝔼 u : (Fin m → F), ffVecChar (p := p) (F := F) v u =
   194	      if v = 0 then (1 : ℂ) else 0 := by
   195	  calc
   196	    𝔼 u : (Fin m → F), ffVecChar (p := p) (F := F) v u =
   197	        if ffVecChar (p := p) (F := F) v = 0 then (1 : ℂ) else 0 :=
   198	      AddChar.expect_eq_ite _
   199	    _ = if v = 0 then (1 : ℂ) else 0 := by
   200	      by_cases hv : v = 0
   201	      · have hzero :
   202	            ffVecChar (p := p) (F := F) v = 0 := by
   203	          subst v
   204	          ext u
   205	          simp [ffVecChar, ffDotProduct]
   206	        rw [if_pos hzero, if_pos hv]
   207	      · have hvc : ffVecChar (p := p) (F := F) v ≠ 0 :=
   208	          ffVecChar_ne_zero (p := p) (F := F) hv
   209	        simp [hv, hvc]
   210	
   211	end Vector
   212	end Fourier
